Creators and Appearances

Creators

Stan Lee, Jack Kirby

First

Incredible Hulk #1
(March, 1962)

The angrier I get, the stronger I get! I'm the strongest one there is!

—Hulk[source]

Dr. Bruce Banner is a nuclear physicist who, after being bombarded by gamma radiation, has become the incredible monster named the Hulk, whose indestructible strength manifests as the personification of his anger. Recruited by General Thunderbolt Ross, Banner was accidentally exposed to the radioactivity of the Gamma Bomb he had designed by saving the life of Rick Jones, a teenager who had inadvertently made his way onto the test site on a dare. Since then, whenever experiencing rage, he turns into a monstrous green goliath who manifests alternative and repressed aspects of his personality. Fearful of the damage that the Hulk could cause, Banner constantly goes on the run to flee from the military, seeking peace in isolation. Moreover, he has a complex and tumultuous relationship with his former employer's daughter, Betty Ross.[2] Sharing his life with the savage Hulk, Bruce Banner has become a loner, struggling to be left alone.[77]

In the years that followed, he occasionally joined together with super-heroes, such as becoming a founding member of the Avengers,[38] though he soon proved to be a problematic team player early on,[78] and also finding belonging with the band of independent outsiders known as the Defenders,[79][80] establishing deep connections with other outsiders.[81] In general, the Hulk is a controversial figure and has explored different approaches to fit in with the world with his different personalities, such as the disreputable Joe Fixit,[40] the stable Professor, who is an integrated version of his personas,[22] and the vicious Green Scar, who declared war against Earth following the destruction of the planet Sakaar.[82][83]

After so many instances of representing a dangerous presence in the universe, Banner was ultimately executed by the expert archer Hawkeye as the culmination of a plan of his own design.[69] Death has not welcomed the immortal Hulk, however, since he has shown an eerie connection with the afterlife, always being resurrected from the dead in spite of everything that is done to him.[84][85][86] As an independent agent, Hulk roamed the planet to protect it from the harm caused by humanity.[87] More recently, the Hulk has resumed his incessant inner conflict against Banner, being constantly entangled in bizarre and horrific events that have separated them.[88] Corrupted by Eldest, Hulk now leads an existence as an infernal creature, marking the emergence of an age of monsters upon Earth.[89]

History

Early Life[]

Robert Bruce Banner was the only son of Dr. Brian Banner, an atomic physicist, and his wife, Rebecca. An abusive man and an alcoholic, Bruce's father was also a well-known researcher of atomic energy at the Los Alamos research base. Years before Bruce was born, Brian was exposed to gamma radiation after an attempt to make a machine to create clean gamma energy went awry. He believed that this incident altered his D.N.A.[90] A selfish man, Brian was convinced by his wife to have a child and soon became jealous of his unborn son; he also began harboring delusions that the radiation that he was exposed to through his research had mutated his son into an abomination.[5] Bruce was born at Ohio General Hospital in Dayton, Ohio. His birth was a complicated one, requiring a Caesarean section in order to save both Bruce and Rebecca's life. The birth was a success, despite Brian's attempts to prevent it from being completed. Not even seeing his newborn child could convince Brian that his son was normal. After many weeks in the hospital, Bruce was eventually allowed to go home with his mother and father.

While Rebecca loved her newborn child, Brian still considered him to be a monster and hated him for taking attention away from his wife. One of Bruce's earliest comforts was a star mobile that was hung over his crib. Brian frequently took his wife out of the house on important social functions, leaving Bruce in the care of his abusive nanny, Nurse Meachum. The only "friend" that Bruce had was his beloved stuffed doll named Guardian. Bruce was both physically and verbally abused by his father for years.[91] Growing up as a child, Banner felt very unloved by his parents.[92] However, Banner was a curious and intelligent child whose curiosity often came to harm, such as when he burned his hand on a radiator as a small infant.[93]

One Christmas Eve when Bruce was 4 years old, he went into the family den in the middle of the night to take a look at the Christmas gifts and could not resist opening the one from his mother. It was a metal building set and while he was entrapped in play, he was caught by his father. Seeing the complicated construct, Brian Banner was convinced that it was proof that his son was somehow genetically altered and would use his superior intelligence to edge out humanity. Rebecca got into the middle of the fight and was slapped. Bruce tried to throw himself at his father, but the 4-year old was easily knocked aside. The commotion woke up Nurse Meachum, who was ordered by Brian to bring Bruce back to bed.[91] Bruce was often isolated to his room while his mother and father went out, soon growing to resent how often they left him alone; however, he came to rely on no one but himself. While he outwardly pretended to be glad whenever his parents left him alone, he secretly cried for them to come back.[94] As Bruce got older, his father continued to be physically abusive toward him.[95] One of his few childhood friends came when he first met his cousin, Jennifer Walters,[96] with whom Bruce used to spend summers in the public library reading for hours, both of them losing themselves in books.[97]

Finally, Rebecca had enough of the constant abuse from her husband and packed up a bag for her and Bruce to try to leave. However, they were caught in the driveway and Brian beat his wife to death in a fit of rage before Bruce's eyes. Upon witnessing his mother's death, Bruce stifled all of his emotions thereafter.[22] Brian was arrested for murdering his wife; however, before the trial Bruce was bullied and abused by Brian into telling the judge and the jury that he had made up his testimony against his father and that his mother had really died by accident when she tripped and fell while trying to flee from her husband.[98] Brian Banner was originally cleared of all charges, until he was overheard confidently gloating about browbeating his son into making a false testimony. Found guilty by reason of insanity, Brian Banner was hauled off to a psychiatric facility for treatment.[99]

Bruce was then placed in the care of his aunt, Susan Drake, who raised Bruce throughout the rest of his childhood.[91] Susan understood Bruce's great pain and rage over his childhood sufferings and raised him with love and care, as if he were her own child. Susan never wanted to see or even deal with her brother again after what he had done to both Rebecca and Bruce. Bruce grew up as a highly withdrawn, intellectually gifted youth; in fact, a child prodigy. Both the traumatic events and his unique genes caused Bruce to start to develop dissociative identity disorder, which he would not be diagnosed with until years later; some of the personalities of which were reflected from himself, and some which were reflected from others, especially at an early age. Despite this, none of these personalities would manifest until years later.[100] The first sign that Bruce was developing mental problems due to his childhood abuse manifested when Bruce began talking to an imaginary friend that he called "Hulk", as a way with coping with his physical abuse, his mother's death and his loneliness.[101] Concerned, his Aunt Susan took him to mental health professionals, who assured her that these were merely coping mechanisms and that they would eventually go away. Unfortunately for the world, they never did, and the Hulk endured as Banner's "imaginary friend" for years.[102]

High School[]

As a teenager, Bruce had visits from his Cousin Jennifer every summer, and the two bonded as though they were brother and sister.[103] Bruce attended Science High School, where he excelled in his work but usually kept to himself, which was a cause for concern among the faculty. One day, one of his classmates tampered with one of his experiments, causing it to explode in his face and getting him in trouble with his science professor.[91] Banner was still a clumsy student, however; as he learned to master science, he was just as prone to cause experiments to blow up in his face as the other students were in deliberately sabotaging his work.[93]

Still relying on the Hulk for guidance, Bruce began to mutter to himself in conversation with his "imaginary friend",[101] as well as keeping detailed notebooks with all sorts of strange equations,[102] thus alienating himself even more from his classmates, who began to think that he was crazy.[101] Bruce also began secretly working on explosives in an abandoned warehouse as a means of venting his frustrations and secretly harboring ideas of revenge against his classmates.[104] Banner frequently made minor errors in his calculations, something that would come back to bite him in the near future. Bruce also developed an infatuation with a fellow classmate named Carla, who was constantly harassed by Ken, one of Bruce's prime tormentors in school.[101] One day in the cafeteria, Bruce saw Carla being harassed again and decided to get involved. Instead of being the knight in shining armor that he had hoped to be, Bruce was knocked out when he was struck in the head with a lunch tray and dragged out into the parking lot, where he was beaten up by his tormentors. Bruce was hospitalized with three broken ribs, a broken nose, two black eyes, and one tooth knocked out. However, his aunt, who had just recently gone through a divorce herself, was unable to get the school administrators to punish the boys responsible due to both the hearsay nature of the claim and the revelations of both Bruce's "imaginary friend" and his notebooks.[102]

When Bruce returned to school, the Hulk tried to warn him that everyone in school would now consider him an even bigger freak than they did before. Bruce ignored his "imaginary friend" and tried to reconnect with Carla, who was now furious at Banner for getting involved in her business. She angrily rejected him for his help because it had made people believe that she was his girlfriend, and how repulsive she thought that was because she now thought of him as much of a freak as everyone else in school did. Bruce was devastated by this rejection, but the Hulk had a solution to this and all of the other wrongs that had been done to Bruce. The Hulk suggested that Bruce smash all his enemies.[104] While Bruce was initially receptive when the Hulk suggested that they blow up the school with the explosives that Bruce had been experimenting with, Bruce suddenly changed his mind and refused to do so, but the Hulk told Bruce that it would happen no matter what, whether he liked it or not. Over the next few nights Bruce was too depressed to attend school, which his aunt allowed. However, unbeknownst to Bruce, when he slept the Hulk took control of his body and planted a bomb in the school that would go off the next morning. When Bruce realized what had happened, he rushed to school to try and disarm it.[105]

Bruce rushed into the school warning everyone about the bomb, but found that no one was listening to him. Crashing into the boiler room, Bruce managed to get down into the basement in just enough time to disarm the bomb. Caught in the boiler room by some of his fellow students, they immediately figured out who planted the bomb and jumped him. The principal then closed the school for the day and locked Bruce down in the boiler room, where he was beaten by the students, who were acting under the principal's orders, until the authorities arrived. Bruce's Aunt Susan agreed that she and Bruce would move out of town in order for Bruce to avoid jail time once he was released from the hospital. Unbeknownst to Bruce, Susan was approached by General Thaddeus E. "Thunderbolt" Ross, a representative of the military, who pointed out to her that the bomb, while sophisticated, was not constructed properly, but the work had impressed the military, who informed Susan that they would invest in his education in the hopes that he could become a great weapons designer who could work for the military.[106]

Further Education[]

After graduating from Science High School, Banner attended medical school before switching to study nuclear physics.[107] in Navapo, New Mexico at Desert State University as the star student of Professor Herbert Josiah Weller.[108] His college roommate was Peter Corbeau.[109] There, he dated a girl named Sally Moore and carved her name on a tree.[108] Later, he dated a girl named Susan Jacobson, but their relationship soon became rocky when Bruce lacked any sort of intimacy and she broke it off after one night where he he aggressively grabbed her arm.[110]

Bruce later transferred to Pennsylvania State University, where he briefly worked with Canadian student Walter Langkowski, finding in him a similar interest in gamma radiation.[111] He also worked with Peter Corbeau and Raoul Stoddard. It was during his time at Penn State that Banner found inspiration from noted scientist Albert Einstein and, like the famous scientist, bought a whole wardrobe consisting entirely of purple suits.[66] Bruce finally finished his education at the California Institute of Technology, where he worked alongside fellow researcher Philip Sterns, who would later become the Madman. It was here that Banner obtained his doctorate in nuclear physics.[66]

As a young student, Bruce first met another student with a brilliant mind: Tony Stark. They both attended Dr. Derenik Zadian's "Forward Thought Conference" at Oxford University.[112] The two became intellectual rivals, although Tony's family wealth and playboy lifestyle eventually distracted him from further competition.[113]

In his final years at school, Bruce met and fell in love with Angela Lipscombe, and the two began dating. They had a promising relationship with their educational backgrounds, and Angela helped Bruce come out of his shell. However, while Angela succeeded in getting scholarship grants, Bruce had great difficulty and his anger and frustration over this began to boil to the surface. Having grown jealous of her success and attributing it to her being attractive, Bruce abruptly ended their relationship and cut off all contact with her.[114]

Gamma Bomb Project[]

As a genius in nuclear physics, Banner wished to pursue philanthropic brands of science, but could not receive any financial funding for his projects;[112] thus, in lack of other options, he went to work at a United States Defense Department nuclear research facility at Desert Base, New Mexico. There, Banner met General Thaddeus E. "Thunderbolt" Ross, the Air Force officer in command of the base. Banner designed and oversaw construction of the "Gamma Bomb" or "G-bomb," a nuclear weapon possessing a high gamma radiation output.[2] Ross still had a critical opinion of Banner, calling him both a "milksop" and a "weakling" and constantly demanding results. Upon finding Guardian among Banner's belongings, Ross was even more disparaging, unintentionally ripping the arm off the stuffed animal. Despite this rough start, Banner began to continue his work on the Gamma Bomb project.[91]

While Bruce intended to develop his bomb as a means of destroying enemy weapons and buildings but sparing human lives, Ross was only interested in making a destructive weapon that would make America's enemies fear them. On the day that Bruce took the job with the military, he was contacted by the mental hospital where his father had been kept for years. He went to see his father and was told that he was cured, and his father also appeared repentant of his past crimes and begged his son to allow him back in his life. Despite his initial misgivings and his inability to trust his father, Bruce agreed to take his father in. However, Bruce noticed that the longer his father stayed with him, the more mentally unstable he became and he became suspicious that his father might be trying to kill him. When Ross learned that Bruce's father had come to live with him, he warned Bruce that the fact that he was allowing a known murderer to live with him could be a security risk, but Bruce told Ross to mind his own business and then left the house, unaware that his father was following him.[99]

Bruce went to visit his mother's grave, as it was the anniversary of her murder. He was confronted by his father, who revealed that he was not as cured of his mental illness as he had led the psychiatric hospital to believe. Still holding onto the notion that his son might be a mutant, Brian attacked his son.[91] Brian knocked Bruce down, while on the ground, Bruce pushed Brian back with his foot. Brian stumbled back and the impact of his head on Rebecca's gravestone killed him instantly. Bruce fled the scene and, thanks to the rainstorm, all evidence placing him at the scene was erased. Bruce reported his father missing and when the police found his body, they wrote it off as a mugging gone horribly wrong.[99] To cope with the fact that he had killed his own father, Bruce blocked the memories of Brian's stay with him and his subsequent death, making himself believe that, as the two of them fought at Rebecca's grave, Brian had simply beat him up and left, later being killed by muggers.[91]

Banner then began pitching his Gamma Bomb project to the United States government. This was a means to an end for Banner, as he hoped that the weaponizing of his gamma research could lead to it being used in other areas, such as medicine to cure disease. However, Banner intentionally made the bomb not nearly as powerful as it could have been, and his frequent tweaking of the bomb prompted military brass and government officials to become uneasy with the amount of taxpayer dollars that were being spent on the project. Banner's project would have been cancelled if it were not for a charismatic entrance and endorsement from Tony Stark, who stood by Banner's work. However, things became sour when Stark pointed out areas where the bomb could be improved. This led to an argument between Banner and Stark, which soured their relationship.[113]

It was during his research in developing the Gamma Bomb that he began working with a technician and became very close to him and his wife. When the technician and his wife gave birth to a young girl named Po, they made Banner the godfather of the child. Uninterested in the child at first, Banner soon came to think highly over her and enjoyed answering her questions about the nature of the world that she lived in; however, he was slightly troubled by her infatuation with death. Tragedy struck when the technician and Po died in a plane crash, their deaths deeply upsetting Banner, who attended their funeral before continuing his work on the Gamma Bomb.[115] On the days leading up to the test of the Gamma Bomb, Banner was becoming deeply troubled by the increase in military observers who had become interested in his project;[114] One of these top brass individuals was General John Ryker.[116]

Meanwhile, Ross had hired Tony Stark to try to alter the bomb in order to make it more powerful. Stark, in turn, tried to get Banner's permission before he began. Banner believed that Stark was trying to get recognition for the Gamma Bomb and tossed Stark out, unaware that Stark intended to both research on and alter the bomb anyway.[117] When asked by Stark why he built the Gamma Bomb, Banner said that he wanted to use gamma energy to power the world, but got no funding and had to transform it into a weapon in order to get government funding.[112] Upon examination, Stark realized that the shielding that Banner put on the bomb to dampen its blast actually made the bomb more powerful and threatened to destroy the entire test site. After lessening the shielding, Stark also found the properties of the gamma rays' output by the bomb could cause mutagenic properties in whatever survived the blast. Later that night, Stark sent an email confessing everything that he had done. However, when Banner received the message, he was so furious that he refused to read it, deleted the message, and blocked Stark from all of his contacts.[118]

On the day before the testing of the Gamma Bomb, Banner was called to Ross' residence to discuss the matter. While Ross was speaking to Major Glenn Talbot on the phone, the door was answered by his daughter, Betty Ross. At first not even looking Banner in the eye, she finally paid attention to him after he helped her with an equation for her graduate course. The two then formed a connection, even with the Hulk in Banner's head belittling him all the while.[119]

Becoming the Hulk[]

Unknown to military staff at the time, one of Banner's assistants, Igor Starsky, was really a Russian spy who was seeking to obtain Banner's plans for the bomb. Banner kept the plans a well-kept secret, but let slip that he had them hidden in his cabin. As the final countdown began, Banner noticed a teenage boy named Rick Jones driving out into the testing area to play his harmonica on a dare from other teenagers. Banner told Igor to delay the countdown while he rushed off to get Rick out of the testing area. However, Igor saw this as an opportunity to get a hold of Banner's plans and allowed the countdown to continue. Banner got to Rick and threw him into a lead-lined trench. However, before he could throw himself to safety, the Gamma Bomb went off, , and intense waves of radiation reached the surface. Banner was irradiated with highly charged radioactive particles.[2]

Banner died, but the Gamma Bomb had created a metaphysical barrier called the Green Door that connected Earth with the Below-Place, the bottom layer of the Multiverse. The Green Door brought Banner back to life, but the time span between his death and resurrection was so short and so fast that his death went completely unnoticed.[55] The Gamma Bomb also mutated Banner's body, causing him to frequently transform into the vastly powerful humanoid monster.[2] According to the later psychiatric work of Dr. Leonard Samson, the Gamma Bomb spawned multiple personalities in Banner's mind. Thanks to the gamma rays' effect on his brain, these personalities manifested in his transformations. These identities were split into the three layers of his identity: the superego (Banner the scientist), the ego (the gray-skinned brutish Hulk) and the id (the green-skinned simple-minded Hulk). During his early transformations into the Hulk, there was a struggle between the ego and id versions of the Hulk. Based on Samson's writings, he has stated that Gray Hulk was the dominant personality during his early transformations, even though his skin was later green, but ultimately the green-skinned Hulk's mind exerted dominance.[22][76]

Chronal Interferences[]

The accident that birthed the Hulk was of such historical significance that it has been the subject of various incidents of tampering from time travellers. Many years in the future on Earth-9200, a the Hulk of Earth-616 battled his evil Earth-9200 counterpart, the Maestro. The battle ended when the Maestro was thrown through Doctor Doom's Time Platform and sent back in time to Earth-616 at the moment of the Gamma Bomb's explosion. The explosion seemingly atomized the Maestro;[120] however, his spirit endured and formed a link between himself and the past Banner.[121]

Another incident was due to a complex plot by Zarrko the Tomorrow Man, a time traveller from the future of Earth-6297, who aligned himself with the Chronarchist known as Khotto in a plot to create an even more powerful Hulk to be used as a weapon.[122] To this end, Zarrko appeared a number of years into the modern era and tricked the spy agency S.H.I.E.L.D. and its sister agency, T.I.M.E., to send the Hulk (one of their operatives in that era) to various points in the past to stop the various Chronanarchists. In order to better command the Hulk, Banner's mind was transferred into a Recording Observation Bot to guide the near-mindless Hulk through the various eras.[123]

The last stop was the day of the Gamma Bomb test that created the Hulk. By this point, previous damage to the timestream had made it so any changes in the past would not create an alternate reality as it originally did, but instead change the course of history itself. Seeing the opportunity to prevent himself from becoming the Hulk, the R.O.B. carrying Banner's mind knocked both his past self and Rick Jones into the trench, saving both their lives. However, the future Hulk was caught in the Gamma Bomb's blast and was mutated into an even stronger version, as per Zarrko's plans.[124] Now with the memories of his future self, Banner saw that, in trying to save himself, he had unleashed a more dangerous threat upon the world — a paradoxical Hulk that was even more powerful than the original one. Banner attacked Khotto and used Zarrko's time window to set time backward to moments before the bomb's explosion and, with the help of the Red She-Hulk, defeated Khotto and set history back on its proper course.[122]

The First Transformations[]

Banner and Rick were recovered by the military, and Banner did not stop screaming in agony for many hours. Left in isolation to presumably die of radiation poisoning, both men survived. However, that night, Banner suddenly transformed into a powerful gray-skinned monster that Ross named "Hulk", unknowingly using the name of Banner's imaginary friend.[2] Upon his transformation, the brutish Hulk smashed out of quarantine and fought his way through the military to get to freedom. Rick, feeling indebted to Banner for saving his life, went after the Hulk to make sure that no one got hurt. The Hulk then went to Betty's house (Banner would later call this moment the first time that he and the Hulk were actually thinking the same thing) and knocked on the door. Betty opened it, thinking that it was her father, but upon realizing it was the Hulk she began screaming at him and demanded to know what the Hulk had done to Banner. Betty then fainted into the Hulk's arms, and Hulk was suddenly surrounded by the Army. The Hulk easily defeated the Army and left. The next morning, Banner was awakened in the desert by Rick, where he had apparently fainted. When Banner asked Rick how he had found him, Rick showed Banner a trail of destruction left from the Hulk's battle with the Army, causing Banner to realize that he was now dangerous as the Hulk. Banner refused Rick's offer to go to the latter's house, unwilling to put someone else in danger; however, Rick pointed out that they had to be together since Banner had saved Rick's life. Banner and Rick then went to a cave with a room that could contain the Hulk, and Banner instructed Rick how to operate a mechanical door to lock the scientist inside, ordering Rick not to let him out unless it was Banner's voice asking to be let out and not the Hulk's. Banner then entered the room, soon turned into the Hulk and inevitably smashed his way out in order to get free to kill Banner, whom he believed was the one who had caged him in the first place.3

Later, Hulk discovered that Rick had been captured by the Army for questioning and attacked the base to rescue him, but he took Betty instead, and was attacked by Iron Man, who was there to rescue Betty. Hulk, believing that Iron Man was a robot, attacked him without mercy and was soon at the verge of killing him; he only stopped when he injured Betty after she tried to stop him from killing Iron Man. Hulk then took Betty to heal her and, after escaping from the police when Hulk went for medicine for Betty, left Betty in a cave and took care of her before being found by the Army. Hulk fought the Army and nearly killed Ross, who was there, until Betty begged Hulk to not do it; Hulk then left. The next morning, Hulk reverted back to Banner, and Rick found Banner in the desert; they managed to get some clothes for Banner and returned to the base, with Banner knowing that he could not let the people believe that the Hulk had killed him; there, Banner was confronted by Ross, who demanded to know about Banner's disappearance.6.

The next time that Banner turned into the Hulk, he tore a path of destruction all the way to his lab, where he caught Igor trying to steal his Gamma Bomb plans. Igor was no match for the brute strength of the Hulk and was easily subdued. When Rick tried to get Hulk to understand that he was really Banner, Hulk rejected Banner as a weakling. However, as the Sun began to rise, Hulk reverted back to Banner before the military arrived. With Igor in custody, the spy used a micro-transmitter hidden under his fingernail to contact his commander, the gamma-mutated Gargoyle. As the Gargoyle smuggled himself into America, Bruce and Rick tried to flee into the desert before nightfall in case Banner transformed into the Hulk again. When Banner transformed into the Hulk once again, he crossed paths with Betty, who had gone looking for Banner, worried about his well-being, and she fainted at the sight of Hulk. The Gargoyle appeared and used his mind control pellets to subdue Hulk and Rick in order to smuggle them into Russia. However, as their rocket crossed the globe into daylight, Hulk reverted back to Banner. The Gargoyle was more impressed with capturing Banner and secreted him away to a lab. However, there the Gargoyle lamented about his mutation and asked Banner for help to be restored to normal. Banner helped the Gargoyle and succeeded in restoring him to his human form. In thanks, the former Gargoyle helped Banner and Rick escape back to America, sacrificing his life to do so in the process.[2]

Early Adventures[]

The following nightly transformation of Banner into Hulk yielded a new version of the Hulk, this one with green skin. Going on a rampage, he was quickly stopped by Rick. Soon, the world was threatened by the Tribbitites hile Bruce and Rick were busy constructing a secret lab and holding place for the Hulk hidden within a cave in the middle of the New Mexican desert. Seeking a brilliant mind to use for their own ends, the Tribbitites kidnapped Banner and Rick. When Bruce refused to help, they shot Rick back to Earth, but as the ship shifted over to the dark side of Earth, Banner transformed into the Hulk once again and trashed their ship. The ship crashed back on the light side of Earth in New Mexico, and Banner was arrested, believed by Ross to be a traitor in league with the Tribbitites. While Banner was incarcerated, the Tribbitites threatened to crash the Moon into the Earth. That night, Banner turned into the Hulk again and broke out of his cell. Seeking revenge against Ross, he went to his home, only to find Betty there. Rick arrived with the military, but Hulk fought them off and fled with Betty back to his lab. There, Rick confronted Hulk to ask for his help, but with the rising of the Sun, Hulk reverted back to Banner. Banner then redeemed himself by using his gamma ray cannon to invert the magnetic weapons of the Tribbitites, sending their fleet spiralling out into outer space and saving Earth from destruction.[125]

Hulk's next transformation had him revert back to his gray form and he was attacked by the Distorter, who used his mind control helmet to make Hulk attack military installations around New Mexico. However, Hulk was ultimately able to resist the Distorter's device and easily defeat him, turning the rogue scientist over to the military.[126] With his underground lab and confinement cell completed, Banner began being placed in captivity at night. When he turned into Hulk again, he once more turned into the green-skinned version, a form that Banner would maintain in one way or another for quite some time. Around this time, Rick was forced to lure Hulk back to Desert Base in order to be used as a test subject for a new manner of rocket. Although Rick managed to load Hulk into the rocket, the military did not intend to return Hulk to Earth. Rick tampered with the controls, sending Hulk crashing to Earth; however, a strange side effect linked Hulk to Rick so that Hulk obeyed all of Rick's verbal commands. However, whenever Rick went to sleep Hulk went on a rampage, forcing Rick to still use the secret chamber to lock up Hulk. During one of the periods in which Rick was awake, he decided to visit a circus. Unknown to him, it was run by the Circus of Crime and when their leader, the Ringmaster, hypnotized Rick along with the rest of the crowd, he was able to send a mental command to Hulk for help in time. Hulk easily quashed the Circus of Crime and he and Rick escaped when the military arrived.[127]

With Banner remaining in his Hulk form since the rocket malfunction, Rick eventually brought Hulk back to the secret lab, where he exposed Hulk to one of Banner's Gamma Ray Projectors in an attempt to change him back to normal. Rick succeeded, but Banner was greatly weakened. After adjusting the device, Banner was able to expose himself to another dose of gamma rays that reverted him back into the Hulk but now with his own mind; however, Banner had a cruel streak. Hulk used his powers to good use, saving a family from a burning house before returning to his lab and changing back into Banner, feeling even weaker than before. With Banner's intellect, Hulk could focus on real threats in the hopes of earning a good name.[128]

When an apparent alien calling himself Mongu came to Earth issuing a challenge to the mightiest person on Earth, Hulk clashed with the "alien" in the Grand Canyon, only to find out that it was really a Russian agent wearing a mechanical suit. Although Hulk defeated "Mongu", the Russians managed to escape, and the military was left to believe that the entire incident was a hoax that had been masterminded by the Hulk.[128] Hulk was next tricked into venturing into the realm of Subterranea by the near-immortal and former Roman ruler Tyrannus, who kidnapped Betty and absconded with her to his underground realm. Hulk was forced to fight in a gladiatorial arena, but the Green Behemoth managed to defeat all of Tyrannus' minions, free himself, Betty and Rick and return to the surface. Later, when the Asian principality of Lhasa was threatened by the Communist soldier known as General Fang, Hulk and Rick travelled to the remote region to defend it from Fang's invasion. Hulk easily quashed Fang's army and then left the general on an American-occupied island to be apprehended.[129]

Back in New Mexico, Hulk was being blamed for a number of acts of sabotage around Desert Base. Furious, Ross hired the Fantastic Four to stop Hulk. Banner, meanwhile, knew that he was innocent and became Hulk to find the real saboteur. This led to a clash with the Fantastic Four and the first of Hulk's many battles with the group's powerhouse, the Thing. With help from Rick, the Fantastic Four and Hulk exposed the real saboteur, a Communist agent calling himself the Wrecker. While Hulk escaped capture again, the Fantastic Four captured the Wrecker and turned him over to the authorities.[130] During this time, Hulk was pulled forward in time to assist Aron the Rogue Watcher against the Fantastic Four and Fantastic Force. When Aron was defeated, all his thralls were returned to their proper times and places with no memory of what had happened to them.[131]

After escaping military capture again, Hulk returned to his secret lab and when he used his gamma ray projector to return to Banner, he was surprised to find that although human in form, his strength was greatly increased. Earth was soon threatened by the Metal Master, an alien who could control metal with his mind. When Banner exposed himself to gamma rays again, all but his head turned into his Hulk form. Fortunately, Banner had made a mask of Hulk's face and wore it. During his first bout with the Metal Master, Hulk was defeated and knocked out. When military personnel arrived on the scene and removed Hulk's latex mask, Banner's incomplete transformation had finished, covering up his secret identity before it could be revealed. With the aid of Rick's newly formed group, the Teen Brigade, Hulk constructed a phony weapon to trick the Metal Master into thinking that Hulk had a metal weapon that was immune to his power. Hulk then easily defeated the Metal Master in combat and forced him to both leave Earth and promise never to return again. For defeating the Metal Master, Hulk was awarded a Presidential pardon; however, when he returned to his lab to change back into Banner, he was horrified to find that the Gamma Ray Projector no longer worked. Losing his temper, Hulk smashed the device; however, his anger triggered the transformation, changing him back into Banner once again.[132]

When Banner next transformed into the Hulk, he was reduced to a blind rage due to a burning sensation under his skin that was a side effect of his transformation. During his rampage, Hulk clashed with the super-hero the Sentry, whose own power had a soothing effect on Hulk and also began a slow transformation in Hulk, making him more intelligent, docile, and able to revert both to and from Banner and Hulk at will. The two became partners of sorts and Hulk spent a time living in New York City within the Sentry's headquarters, the Watchtower. The duo clashed with foes such as the General, the Living Nuke, and the Lobster People. When Hulk risked his life to save the Lobster People's colony, he was heralded as a hero. Also, for his part in stopping the Lobster People's invasion of the surface world, Hulk was also heralded as a hero; however, during the parade in Hulk's honor, the Sentry's old foe the Void attacked and when Hulk tried to defend his friend, the Void attacked Hulk with his tendrils. Hulk then fell to the ground, where he was in a coma for days. When Hulk awoke, the battle was over and both the Sentry and the Void were gone. Without the Sentry's influence, the burning sensation came back to Hulk and he reverted back to his brutish mentality.[133]. Later, the Sentry made everyone forget his existence; as such, for many years no one remembered the Sentry or his past and, also as such, Hulk's brief time as a celebrity was also forgotten.[134].

Ultron Forever[]

Hulk, along with other heroes from different time periods, were then abducted by the "Doctor Doom" of an alternate future where Ultron had successfully taken over the world. Doom asked the heroes to help him free the world from Ultron's control, to which they complied. While the Vision and Iron Man distracted the A.I. Avengers, Hulk, alongside the Black Widow and Captain America, infiltrated the Avengers Tower, but were ambushed by Ultron's version of the Black Widow and her Bio-Slaves, and managed to decapitate Hulk using Captain America's anti-gravity shield.[57]

Despite this, Hulk was able to survive the beheading through Banner's head emerging from Hulk's neck. Banner explained that he had done experiments to rid Hulk from himself, which might have caused further mutations. Banner then reattached Hulk's head to his body and the two heads began fighting the reactivated Bio-Slaves. As Ultron's factories began shutting down thanks to the heroes' efforts, Doom recalled them and revealed that he had taken over Ultron's system, thus becoming the new ruler of the world. He tried to send the heroes back to their respective times, but Thor managed to evade that attempt and hide within this timeline.[58] Arriving at Asgardia, Doom sent billions of Ultron Drones to attack them. They were hardly able to destroy one ship carrying the sentinels as other ships arrived. Luckily, Iron Man managed to free the imprisoned Asgardians, who then joined in the battle. After that, the heroes went to Doom, who was revealed to have been a Doombot all along and was convinced by the Vision to free the imprisoned humans and become their kindhearted leader. Afterward, all of the heroes were returned to their own times.[135]

Joining the Avengers[]

Hulk soon became a means to an end for the Asgardian trickster god Loki to get revenge against his step-brother, Thor. To this end, Loki tricked Hulk into damaging a railroad track. Although Hulk prevented the train from getting wrecked, he was blamed for the destruction of the track and hunted by the authorities.[38] Not wanting Hulk to get hurt, Rick and the Teen Brigade attempted to contact the Fantastic Four; however, Loki intercepted their message and had it go to Thor instead. He also unintentionally caused the message to be received by Iron Man, Ant-Man and his sidekick, the Wasp. The four heroes arrived at the Teen Brigade's headquarters and, after hearing Rick's plea to help Hulk, agreed to band together to stop the gamma-spawned monster.[38] Hulk attempted to lay low by hiding out in a trailer belonging to a circus. He was discovered by the bearded lady, who convinced the owner of the circus to allow Hulk to stay with them.[136]

The circus had Hulk disguise himself as "Mechano", claiming that he was actually a robot. This disguise proved to be short-lived, however, as Ant-Man was able to track down Hulk using his network of ants. The ants caused the ground to cave in under Hulk, keeping him distracted enough for the heroes to catch up with him.[38] A fight broke out, but Hulk still cared enough to save the life of the bearded lady who had helped him find shelter among the circus. With the battle not working out in his favor, Hulk instead bounded away to keep more innocents from being hurt.[137] Hulk fought the heroes in a factory;[138] during the course of the battle, Thor returned from his native Asgard with Loki, revealing him as the true mastermind behind the whole plot to pit them against Hulk. After the battle was over, the group decided to band together as a team, calling themselves the Avengers.[38] Hulk was not originally at the meeting, but he barged in later and convinced the Avengers to let him join their group so he would not have to worry about them hounding him again.[139]

A Short-Lived Avenger[]

After the Avengers were publicly unveiled,[140] Hulk's tenure with the Avengers proved to be very short-lived. During Hulk's initial visit to what eventually became known as Avengers Mansion, he frightened away all of the staff, leaving behind only Tony Stark's butler, Edwin Jarvis, who loyally stayed on the job.[141] When Iron Man attempted to get government sanctions for the Avengers, Hulk's membership in the group turned out to be an absolute public relations nightmare. Hulk and Rick met with the team at the mansion. When discussing a charter and rules for the group, Hulk grew agitated and literally jumped out of the mansion, causing a lot of damage and more negative publicity for the group.[142] Later, the group met to determine who would lead the group; Hulk came to blows with both Thor and Iron Man until, ultimately, the group decided to elect the Wasp as their secret chairperson so as not to bruise the egos of the male members.[143]

Soon after this, the Avengers were asked by the military to stop the Latverian monarch Doctor Doom from recapturing a ship that the military had had in their possession. Although the heroes were lured into a trap aboard the ship by Doom's followers, they managed to destroy the ship. Hulk nearly caught Doom himself, but only succeeded in capturing one of his Doombot simulacrums.[144] An Avengers meeting by Iron Man, Thor and Hulk — was crashed by another time-travelling Iron Man, who arrived with the Doctor Doom of his own era. This pair briefly interacted with Hulk and others before being returned to their own time.[145] The Avengers were next targeted by the Space Phantom, an agent of Immortus, who was manipulating the Avengers' lives in order to ensure that they followed their destined path.[146]

The Space Phantom could take the place of an individual, displacing them to the timeless realm of Limbo while he possessed that person's form. The Space Phantom transformed into the Hulk, shunting him off to Limbo, and both attacked the Avengers and went on a rampage.[147] While there, Hulk crossed paths with future Avengers the Wasp, Hercules and the Black Knight. When Hulk tried to attack, Hercules knocked Hulk out with a single punch and he was whisked back to Earth when the Space Phantom assumed a new form.[148] Although the Avengers eventually learned the truth, Thor had insulted Hulk during the battle and Hulk fled back to the Southwest. There, he and Thor battled it out until Iron Man came and convinced them to return to battle the Space Phantom.[149] After the Space Phantom was defeated, the team's easy mistrust of Hulk made the Green Goliath realize that they feared and distrusted him, so Hulk quit the team.[147] Hulk went on a rampage until he crossed paths with a pregnant woman who was rushing to a hospital alone, as she had gone into labor. Hulk's rage subsided and he helped the woman give birth, but soon passed out and reverted back into Banner. Banner woke up in a prison cell and was interrogated by the police, who believed he was a drunken bum who had murdered someone. However, after hearing his story and having a lab report confirm that the blood on him contained embryonic fluid, he was released from custody.[150]

Hunted by the Avengers[]

After Hulk had abruptly quit the team, the Avengers were determined to hunt him down, not wishing him to run free. Hulk's only ally was Rick, who found Hulk back in the Southwest and helped him return to his secret lab and the Gamma Ray Projector, turning him back into Banner. However, the blast was not strong enough, and Banner changed back into Hulk that night, angrier and more out of control than ever. Rick alerted the Avengers, who came to New Mexico to clash with Hulk. Despite their combined might, the team were unable to capture Hulk, who managed to escape. Hulk managed to escape out to sea, where he found refuge on a small island. There, he was confronted by the Atlantean prince Namor the Sub-Mariner, who was seeking new allies in his war against the surface world.[151]

Despite the fact that both of them held each other in contempt, an uneasy alliance was formed between the two. They then lured the Avengers to an island that held an abandoned military base from World War II, where a battle broke out.[151] During the course of the battle, Hulk and Thor were separated from the other combatants and fought one-on-one. However, there was no clear victor, as their battle caused the cavern that they were fighting in to collapse, separating the two. Hulk then rejoined the battle with Namor against the Avengers.[152] Ultimately, Hulk ended up fleeing the battle when he began to revert back to his human form of Banner and fled so as not to compromise his double identity. Seeing that his ally had abandoned him, Namor then ended the conflict, escaping into the ocean.[151] The Avengers then resumed their hunt for Hulk. Hulk tried to flee the area, using force to sneak onto the back of a truck, where he reverted back into Banner and managed to slip past a military cordon. Later, fleeing back to his secret lab, Banner once more turned into Hulk, who smashed all of Banner's machinery in an attempt to remain the Hulk forever; then, seeking revenge against the Avengers for constantly hounding him, began making his way toward their headquarters in New York City.

The Avengers were still in New Mexico searching for Hulk and so, when word went out that Hulk was heading for the Big Apple, the Fantastic Four were alerted. The team fared poorly defending the city from Hulk; with their leader, Mister Fantastic, ill, both the Invisible Girl and the Human Torch were injured fighting the Jade Giant, leaving the Thing as the only member of the group to stand in the way of Hulk's rampage. Although the Thing lost the first bout, he got back up and continued after Hulk.[153] Hulk was later attacked by the Thing and a partially-recovered Human Torch; outnumbered, Hulk fled through the New York subway system and managed to finally make his way to Avengers Mansion. There, he found the Avengers waiting for him and a battle erupted out into the street. The fully-recovered Fantastic Four arrived and assisted the Avengers in chasing Hulk up a partially-constructed office tower. Hulk was able to hold his own against the two uncoordinated hero teams until Rick managed to throw a gamma-irradiated pill into Hulk's mouth. This knocked Hulk out, causing him to fall into the Hudson River, reverting back into Banner as he was swept away by the currents.[154]

Banner returned to Desert Base, where his frequent and lengthy absences began to make Ross suspicious of Banner's activities outside the base. Despite this, Banner was charged with investigating a strange mound that was growing out of the ground from beneath the base. The Avengers were eventually called in and they clashed with the creators of the mound, the underground-dwelling race of Subterraneans known as the Lava Men. During the Avengers' battle with the Lava Men, Banner transformed into the Hulk once again, entered the underground domain and clashed with his former allies. During the course of the battle, Hulk was tricked into punching the mound as hard as he could, causing a massive explosion that sealed the Lava Men below; the blast also knocked Hulk away from the battle, where he reverted back into Banner. He was found by Betty, who presumed that he had been harmed by Hulk and helped carry him away to safety.[155]

When Banner next transformed into the Hulk, he sought refuge in the caverns below New Mexico. This sanctuary proved short-lived, as he crossed paths with Spider-Man, who had been lured below himself by his foes the Green Goblin and the Enforcers while on a phony film shoot. While Spider-Man defeated the Enforcers and the Green Goblin escaped, Hulk proved too powerful for Spider-Man to fight alone. Although the masked hero managed to hold his own, he was eventually forced to hide in order to avoid further conflict and Hulk went about his business.[156] Before Hulk could land a killing blow on Spider-Man, he was rescued by Captain America, who helped put Hulk down.[157]

Banner returned to New York shortly thereafter and, in need of food, went to the Baxter Building, headquarters of the Fantastic Four, and was admitted into the building by his old sparring partner, the Thing. Banner's visit was cut short when New York was attacked by a legion of monsters that were unleashed by the Mole Man. Banner was forced to transform into the Hulk and Thing convinced Hulk to help him round up the monsters, along with Giant-Man and Beast. Hulk assisted in taking down the monsters Tragg, Groot, Taboo, Grottu, Droom, Vandoom's Monster, Gargantus, Rommbu, and Grogg, and most of the monsters were then banished to the Negative Zone.[158]

Reverting back to human form, a more embittered Banner returned to working at Desert Base. When the Avengers Giant-Man and the Wasp came to the base seeking to help find Hulk and once again convince him to rejoin the Avengers, Ross assigned Banner to help the two heroes, but Banner refused and stormed off into the desert. There, he transformed into the Hulk once again and went on another rampage. While Giant-Man and the Wasp evacuated a nearby town, their recurring foe the Human Top approached Hulk and warned him that the heroes were waiting for him. Hulk then attacked Giant-Man in town while the Human Top then went to tell Ross that Hulk was in the town alone and Ross ordered a nuclear weapon to be used on it. When the Wasp learned that her partner was in the town fighting Hulk, she was able to warn him over the radio. Duly warned, Hulk intercepted the nuclear missile, carrying it away from the town. The radiation from the missile's explosion caused Hulk to revert back to Banner. Banner returned to his work at Desert Base while Giant-Man and the Wasp gave up on their mission and returned to New York City.[159]

When Banner next turned into Hulk, he fled to Antarctica in order to escape the military and find peace; however, the cold weather was too brutal for even Hulk and he collapsed, reverting back into Banner. Fortunately, Banner was rescued by a team of scientists researching the effects of global warming on the hole in the ozone layer over the region. Their investigation also accidentally revived the ancient Makluan dragon Fin Fang Foom. While Foom attempted to obtain a human host to regain his strength, killing some of the scientists in the process, Banner was regarded with some suspicion, triggering his transformation into the Hulk. Seeing this powerful form before him, Foom revealed his true form and Hulk attacked the massive alien dragon. Foom attempted to convince Hulk to join his cause, but Hulk decided that if anyone would rule Earth, it would be Hulk alone, and the Jade Giant promptly tossed the massive dragon to the Moon before departing to be alone again.[160] Hulk also worked with the Sentry again, venturing into the Negative Zone to battle the Irish-themed Danny Boy.[161] Banner's expertise was sought out to assist in stopping the super-villain Sundown who was rampaging through New York City; however, Banner was unavailable at the time due to one of his absences while transformed into the Hulk.[162]

Hulk returned to the Southwest, where the Avengers, joined by Captain America, followed him in the hopes of convincing Hulk to rejoin their ranks. Hulk fought against the Avengers, ignored Rick's pleas and fled. He was then contacted by Baron Zemo and his team, the Masters of Evil, who convinced him to join their cause in destroying the Avengers. Hulk joined Zemo, Skurge the Executioner and Amora the Enchantress in attacking the Avengers, but Hulk turned against Zemo and the Masters when Zemo foolishly threatened Rick's life. Defeated by Hulk, the Masters fled and Hulk, not wishing any further conflict, left the area as well.[163]

Under Suspicion at the Desert Base[]

Banner's frequent absences started taking their toll on him, as it prompted Ross to apply more pressure on Banner to complete his projects, such as a robotic suit of armor that could allow someone to withstand an atomic blast. Banner soon came to realize that his recent spat of transformations were all caused by stress and that similar stress also triggered Hulk's reversion back into human form. Such a situation of stress occurred when Ross gave Banner only a few hours to finish perfecting his robotic battle suit, prompting a transformation into the Hulk. Hulk fled Desert Base, leaving the suit of armor vulnerable to be taken over by a spy. When the spy tried to abscond with the armor during the morning tests, Ross believed that Banner was trying to steal his own invention. The spy clashed with Hulk briefly, but managed to escape when Hulk began reverting back into Banner.[164]

Unable to prove that Banner was involved in the theft of the suit, Ross was forced to let him go free, and Banner soon began building a device that would help him track down the spy who han stolen it. His search for the spy coincided with the arrival of Major Glenn Talbot. Talbot was sent to Desert Base by the Pentagon to investigate suspicions that Banner might be a spy and/or have a connection to the Hulk. Talbot instantly became smitten by Ross' daughter, Betty, becoming determined to expose Banner as a spy or worse in order to eliminate him from the competition for Betty's love. Banner managed to track down the spy who stole the suit of armor and transformed into the Hulk. As they battled, Talbot and Betty arrived on the scene and Talbot shielded her from debris from a rock that had been smashed by Hulk. Hulk succeeded in defeating the spy by knocking him into a seemingly bottomless pit. However, the spy had a back-up plan and had launched a missile at Desert Base. Hulk dived into the path of the missile, detonating it. Hulk was knocked out and Talbot quickly mobilized the military to subdue the green-skinned monster; in a bit of irony, special bonds that had been designed by Banner himself were used to subdue Hulk.[165]

After failing to hear from his spy, the Leader, a gamma radiation-spawned super-genius, sent the international spy the Chameleon to obtain secrets from the base. Also, having heard that the Hulk was captured, Rick briefly left his partnership with Captain America and the Avengers to plead in Hulk's defence. Disguised as Ross, the Chameleon approached the captive Hulk and attempted to obtain an alliance with him. Hulk refused and, while the Chameleon was busy dismissing the guard placed around him, he reverted back into Banner. Easily able to slip out of the special bonds, Banner was found by Rick, who quickly helped him change into some fresh clothes and report in. However, both Ross and Talbot were even more suspicious of Banner in light of Hulk escaping and someone posing as Ross. As Banner left the meeting, he was jumped by the Chameleon, who disguised himself as Banner to gain access to his lab. Hearing Betty in distress, Banner transformed into the Hulk again and attacked the Chameleon, who managed to keep Hulk at bay by threatening to use a Gamma Bomb grenade.[166]

Ultimately the Chameleon ditched Betty and tossed the grenade, but Hulk shielded the blast with his body. The resulting explosive buried the Chameleon in debris, and the gamma rays from the explosion reverted Hulk back to human form. Under the cover of smoke, Banner then fled the scene to change into fresh clothes again. When forced to report to Ross and Talbot, the fact that Betty was able to see through the Chameleon's disguise cleared Banner of any wrongdoing; however, the pair were more determined than ever to pin something, anything, on Banner.[166] Banner was next ordered to be present on a military train shipping his latest invention, the Absorbatron, to its testing area. Talbot was determined to stick to Banner like glue, hoping to learn his secrets. This did not happen, however, as the train was soon attacked by one of the Leader's Humanoids. Talbot locked Banner in a room aboard the train while the military handled the attacker. However, Banner transformed into the Hulk and broke out of the room. Hulk then prevented the Humanoid from stealing the Absorbatron and returned to human form before the military arrived. Finding Banner on the scene, Talbot accused him of being involved in the theft and had him locked up, pending trail.[167]

While incarcerated, Banner was granted a request to be given tranquilizers, which he used to remain in human form so as not to betray his identity. Salvation came from Rick himself, who came to Banner's aid. Seeing that Banner was stuck, Rick used his Avengers priority status to meet with the President of the United States. After confiding Banner's double identity as the Hulk to the President, the President agreed that Banner's secret must be kept, lest enemy nations discover the truth and both attack and capture Banner in order to learn how to create their own versions of the Hulk. Banner was soon given a Presidential pardon, angering Talbot and making him more determined than ever to find some proof that Banner was a traitor to his country. Banner and Talbot were next dispatched to Astra Island, where they were to test the Absorbatron. When Banner realized that he was out of tranquilizers, he fled while transforming into the Hulk. This transformation coincided with the Leader's attempt to steal the Absorbatron with an army of Humanoids.[168]

Hulk fought the Humanoids until the military arrived, prompting the Leader to recall his Humanoids lest they be destroyed. Hulk also attempted to escape by swimming away in the ocean. While Hulk succeeded in escaping the American military, he changed back into Banner and nearly drowned. He was rescued by a Russian submarine and taken to a Communist country in Eastern Europe. There, Banner was informed by the so-called Commandant that he was going to be forced to work for the Soviets. When Banner refused to work for them, he was placed in a small cell, where his stress level increased to the point that it triggered another transformation into the Hulk. Hulk then broke out of his cell and trashed the facility that he was being held in. However, the Commandant called in reinforcements. Wounded by a blast from a "Vaporizer Ray", Hulk was assisted by one of the captive scientists to heal his wounds, but the temperamental Hulk shunned his offers of friendship.[169] It was not until the Commandant slew the scientist that Hulk realized that the man was trying to help and Hulk went on another rampage until his stress triggered another reversion. Banner awakened and had to flee attacking jet fighters, but transformed into the Hulk again when he came across the dead scientist's body, saving him in the nick of time from a missile. Hulk then smashed the fighters and continued on his rampage.[170]

Hulk cut a path of destruction into Russia, but the constant attacks grew on the behemoth's nerves and so he leapt across many miles until he reached Mongolia, where an exhausted Banner reverted back to human form. He was found by Kanga Khan, a Mongolian raider who took Banner prisoner and agreed to contact the American authorities to turn him over for ransom. The military sent Talbot to recover Banner, but his arrival coincided by an attack by Hakun Gantu and his rival tribe on Kanga Khan. Talbot fled with Banner, but while trying to cross a narrow mountain path, it gave way under their feet and they began to fall.[171] While Talbot was knocked out by the fall, Banner was saved thanks to another transformation into the Hulk. As the Hulk, Banner then bounded his way back to America, leaving Talbot behind. Hulk managed to find his way back to Banner's home to rest, where he reverted back into human form. When he awakened, he found Ross, Betty and an army of soldiers looking for him to arrest him. Talbot had been recovered and his request to punish Banner was denied by the President himself. Instead, the pair were ordered to return to Astra Island to complete the test of the Absorbatron. Prior to their arrival, the Leader doused the island with an army of miniaturized Humanoids that grew to full size when Banner and Talbot arrived. Overpowered, Banner transformed into the Hulk and began fighting the creatures off; however, this time the Leader was prepared for the attack and used a powerful knockout gas to put Hulk to sleep and take him prisoner.[172]

The Leader then absconded with Hulk and the Absorbatron, hoping to use both to rule the world. While examining the Hulk, the Leader left him alone to find instruments that could pierce his tough skin. While the Leader was gone, Banner returned to human form and used his intelligence to break free and send out a signal to the military. Finding Hulk missing from the examining table, the Leader tried to flood the room with gas, prompting another transformation by Banner into the Hulk. However, Hulk's strength was too much for the Leader, who fled as Hulk destroyed the Absorbatron before exhaustion overtook him and he returned to his human form. Just then, the military and Rick arrived. Rick attempted to stop the military before Ross' orders to shoot to kill were carried out, but Rick was too late and Banner was seemingly shot dead.[59]

Trapped as the Hulk[]

Although Banner was legally dead, Rick absconded with his body to Banner's secret lab. There, Rick bombarded Banner with the Gamma Ray Projector which triggered his transformation into the Hulk, reviving him and keeping the bullet in his skull from killing him. Hulk realized that he now retained Banner's mind and he was also horrified to realize that, in order to stay alive, he had to remain Hulk at all times. Creating a chemical concoction to remain Hulk for 48 hours, Banner went to Desert Base to get one last look at Betty before leaving his old life completely. However, his arrival coincided with an attack by the Leader's giant Humanoid. Hulk tried to fight the Humanoid, but the military confused his assistance as his being responsible for the attack. This prompted Ross to order the launching of his "Sunday Punch" missile.[60]

Hulk was alerted to the danger by Rick, and he managed to get himself and Rick away from the blast. The attack angered Banner and his mind began to deteriorate. He and Rick retreated back to his secret lab, but they were followed by the military. With Ross ordering Hulk's surrender, he sent Rick out to distract them while he tried to figure out how to get out of this situation. As the military prepared to attack, Hulk was offered salvation from the Leader.[173] Hulk accepted the Leader's offer and was teleported away just as his lab was destroyed, leaving the military to think that Hulk had been killed. Hulk was transported to the Leader's hideout in Greece. The Leader asked Hulk to join him in conquering the world, but Hulk refused. Anticipating this, the Leader felled Hulk with more knockout gas. When Banner later awakened, he began to feel the change that would turn him back into his human form and kill him. Trashing the Leader's lab to try and find a device that utilized gamma rays to sustain his Hulk form, Banner alerted the Leader to his destruction and he unleashed his Humanoids on him.[174]

With Hulk weakening, the Leader called off his Humanoids and, while examining Hulk, the Leader found the bullet and used his gamma-powered machines to dissolve it and save Banner's life. However, as a consequence Banner was horrified to find that although he would live, he was now trapped in the form of the Hulk. The Leader ordered Hulk to assist him in recovering the so-called Ultimate Machine from the homeworld of Uatu the Watcher. Indebted to the Leader for saving his life, Hulk agreed, and the Leader teleported Hulk to Uatu's homeworld. There, Uatu revealed himself, telling Hulk that he would not interfere in his quest. Before Hulk could recover the Ultimate Machine, he was attacked by the alien Amphibion.[175] The Amphibion also sought the Ultimate Machine and the two of them fought it out. Uatu allowed them to fight, only interfering first to teleport them away from his equipment and then to send the Amphibion away when he deemed Hulk to be the winner of the fight. Hulk then claimed the Ultimate Machine and was quickly teleported with it back to Earth by the Leader, who wanted to take no chances of Uatu stopping him. Although the Leader was victorious, when he placed the Ultimate Machine on his head, its collected knowledge proved to be too much for even his enhanced mind, with his brain being overloaded by the device's information.[176]

Hulk left Leader's lair, his mind devolving even more. Back in the United States, Hulk decided to try to use the Ultimate Machine. While it was too powerful for him as well, it still picked up a thought that Rick was under military arrest and demanding to see the President. Hulk abandoned the Ultimate Machine to go to Washington, D.C., with the military trying to oppose his progress. Ross ordered to use the T-Gun, a weapon that had been designed by Banner, on Hulk. When Hulk was blasted with it, it appeared to vaporize him; however, he was actually transported to the 25th century of Earth-6676, a world that had been decimated by a great war. He was instantly attacked by the forces of King Arrkam[177] and taken prisoner. Taken to King Arrkam's fortress, he was told to assist them in their battle against the "Evil One", the Executioner of that era. Hulk initially refused and broke free; however, the Executioner and his forces attacked.[178] Hulk overpowered the Executioner and his forces and sent them fleeing but, despite this, King Arrkam and his forces believed that Hulk had assisted the Executioner in his attack. Before they could attack Hulk, the effects of the T-Gun wore off and he was transported back to his own era and returned to the ruins of his old lab in New Mexico. This happened just moments after a grief-stricken Rick, believing that Banner was dead, had revealed Hulk's identity to Ross and Talbot.[179]

Hulk's return was instantly discovered by the military, who renewed their attack on him. Attacking Desert Base, Hulk was quickly captured thanks to a plan devised by Banner's replacement, Professor Konrad Zaxon. Zaxon, having created a device that could harness the organic energy of Hulk and with aspirations of world domination, attempted to attack Hulk alone.[180] By this point Hulk's mind had devolved to that of a simple brute and, although weakened by Zaxon's weapon, he fought back. Zaxon was knocked aside and caught in the path of his own weapon, killing him. Accused of murdering Zaxon, Hulk fled the base. Going on a rampage, Hulk destroyed a railroad track, stopping a train. Incidentally, the train carried the Olympian demi-god Hercules, who was en route to Hollywood to pursue a film career. Hulk held his own against Hercules, but was forced to flee when the military caught up with him and attacked him again.[181] When the X-Men were recruited by the FBI to hunt down Hulk in the northwest, Rick convinced them that Hulk was a hounded victim. The X-Men let Hulk go when their leader, Professor X, learned that the military intended to weaponize the Hulk.[182]

Hulk managed to find refuge, but his peace was short-lived. He was teleported back to Subterranea by his old foe, Tyrannus. Tyrannus sought Hulk's aid in recovering his Fountain of Youth from the Mole Man in order to restore his youth. Hulk initially refused until Tyrannus revealed that he held Betty, Rick and Talbot as his prisoners. Hulk plowed through the Mole Man's Moloid forces and went toe-to-toe with the Mole Man's war machine, the Octo-Sapien. During the fight Hulk threw the Octo-Sapien into the Fountain of Youth, causing a massive explosion that destroyed the fountain and changed Hulk back into Banner.[183] As Banner fought his way back to Tyrannus' stronghold, he learned that his foe had released his friends and continued on to find his matter transporter. Swarmed by Tyrannus' legion of Tyrannoids, this forced a transformation into the Hulk. Hulk easily fought them off and got to the matter transporter, returning him to the surface.[184]

Secret Empire[]

While Hulk was detained by Tyrannoids on the surface, the terrorist organization Secret Empire sent their agent Boomerang to kidnap Betty in order to ransom her in return for the military's new Orion missile.[184] Hulk's return to the surface was met with another attack by the military. Fleeing, Hulk crossed paths with Boomerang, who was trying to escape with Betty. Unable to shake Hulk, Boomerang was forced to let her go, forcing Hulk to rescue her so that he could escape the scene.[185] Hulk brought Betty to shelter and then went to get her food. He was attacked by the military again, but when he spotted Rick and Ross, Hulk nabbed them and brought them to Betty, who explained that Hulk was not involved in her kidnapping by Boomerang. More frustrated than ever, Hulk bounded away to find peace.[186]

Hulk was briefly transported back in time millions of years to Earth-78411 by the Celestial Gamiel the Manipulator to assist the Killer Folk in forcing the Small Folk from the Valley of Flame and defeating their defenders, Devil Dinosaur and Moon-Boy. Hulk was made leader of the Killer Folk and was convinced to go to battle Devil Dinosaur. Witnessing the battle was Gamiel's rival, Devron the Experimenter, who used his technology to enhance Devil Dinosaur's evolution to make him a match for Hulk. However, the gamma and mutagenic energies exerted by the two combatants were too much for both of them and Gamiel and Devron were forced to imprison Hulk and Devil Dinosaur on their ship. The two then worked together to break free. Unable to control the two powerhouses, the two youthful Celestials were forced to restore Devil Dinosaur, return him to the planet's surface and transport Hulk back to his proper time.[187]

Hulk attempted to find companionship at Desert Base, only to find it mysteriously deserted. Deciding to seek out the Avengers, Hulk then left for New York City. Knowing that people would be scared of him, Hulk stole a trench coat and a hat to disguise himself, but not before he was sighted by the NYPD, who put out a dragnet to find Hulk. Hulk found refuge in a movie theater, but his refuge was put in a panic thanks to the Sub-Mariner happening to be in there as well. Hulk fled into the New York subway system, where he fell on and damaged the third rail and then saved a train before it crashed.[188] Hulk fled to a nearby gamma ray research center. There, he was attacked by Spider-Man, who was on a mission to capture Hulk as part of his admission into the Avengers. During the fight, Hulk rammed his fist into a gamma ray device and reverted back into Banner. Banner pleaded with Spider-Man to stop him, but he changed into Hulk again. With Hulk still weak from the transformation, Spider-Man webbed him up. The Wall-Crawler began to feel sorry for Hulk, and decided instead to let him go and give up his chance of membership in the Avengers.[189]

Hulk continued to rampage across New York and, as coincidence would happen, Hulk was drawn to the building where Number One of the Secret Empire was hiding out. Thinking that Hulk was after him, he set a bomb to go off and attempted to flee out of the building, but his cape got caught in the door outside. When the bomb exploded, Number One was killed, but Hulk escaped unscathed. Hulk was pursued by the authorities until he was found by Rick, who helped him to get to cover. This coincided with the test of the Orion missile, which a spy named Gorki attempted to use a device to redirect it to hit New York City. Rick convinced Hulk to stop the missile, but when Hulk bounded up to the approaching warhead, he reverted back into Banner.[190] Because Banner had designed the Orion missile, he was able to override Gorki's signal and had the missile redirected to splash down into the Atlantic Ocean. Banner changed into the Hulk and was blamed for the missile being overridden. Having discovered one of the Leader's old lairs, the military found and activated his special Humanoid Hulk-Killer and sent it to attack Hulk.[191]

Hulk was unable to beat the Hulk-Killer with his brute strength, but during the fight Gorki was captured and Hulk cleared of all involvement, forcing the military to try to save Hulk. Weakened in the fight, Hulk reverted back into Banner. Banner was then pulled to safety and he developed a device that, as Hulk, he used to overload the Hulk-Killer, destroying it.[192] Hulk was hailed as a hero, but the brutish Hulk was easily agitated. Boomerang, seeking revenge for not getting paid for his job with the Secret Empire, secretly attacked Hulk and made him lash out at the soldiers and press gathered around him. When Hulk bounded away, Boomerang went after him. At first, Boomerang gained the upper hand and blew up a nearby dam. When he went back to gloat at Hulk, Hulk knocked him aside, damaging his rockets and breaking his arm. With the water rushing away, Hulk began reverting back into Banner. Although he attempted to rescue Boomerang, his powers failed and Boomerang fell into the raging water below. Banner, meanwhile, got to safety, where he passed out.[193]

A Pawn of the Stranger[]

Banner was found by the cosmic being known as the Stranger. He sought to use Hulk as his engine of destruction to eliminate human civilization so that he could rebuild Earth and be its leader. Forcing Banner to change into Hulk, the Stranger then used a device to brainwash Hulk into wanting to destroy humanity and left the monster to his work while the Strange dealt with other matters off-world.[194] Hulk went on a small rampage before he transformed back into Banner near Desert Base. Fearing that he would menace humanity if he transformed into the Hulk again, Banner decided to commit suicide by exposing himself to a massive gamma ray blast with one of his devices on the base. His arrival on the base coincided with security being compromised by the Russian spy Emil Blonsky, who was posing as a soldier and searching Banner's old lab. When Banner set up the machine, he was caught by Talbot, who took him into custody. Blonsky then foolishly activated the gamma ray device and was mutated into a massive Gamma Mutate the Abomination. Abomination went on a rampage across the base. Seeing the carnage, Banner turned into the Hulk and tried to battle Abomination; however, Abomination proved to be more powerful than Hulk and nearly beat him to death. Abomination then fled with Betty as a hostage to keep the military at bay.[195]

Knowing that Hulk was the only one who could catch up with Abomination and rescue Betty, he was rushed to a medic. Hulk was revived thanks to the help of Rick, who suggested they use gamma electrodes to revive his friend. Hulk immediately began to go on a rampage, but Rick was able to calm Hulk down enough to make him change back into Banner. Banner then used the military's Infinite Weapon Ray to lure Abomination back to the base. After significantly weakening Abomination, Banner got worked up enough to change back into the Hulk. This time, Hulk was able to defeat Abomination. By this point, the Stranger had returned to Earth and had been moved by the altruistic nature of Hulk and decided to rescind his attempt to conquer Earth. Seeing Abomination as truly evil, the Stranger then teleported him away for reasons of his own. Although Hulk was once again hailed as a hero, the green-skinned brute was uninterested in praise and walked off, wishing to be left alone.[196] Hulk tried to flee the desert, escaped the military and incidentally stopped bank robber Coyote Cash from escaping the authorities.[76]

Wanting to Belong[]

Wanting to be alone, Banner went into seclusion and attempted to build a device to try and cure himself of being the Hulk. However, the device was a failure and he transformed into the Hulk once again. Hulk then tried to flee the city, which went on high alert. Spotting the Silver Surfer passing by, Hulk mistook him for an alien vessel and attempted to "board the ship". When Hulk tried to grab the board, the Surfer blasted him off and confronted him.[197] Hulk battled it out with the Surfer, but the Surfer was too powerful, soon grew weary of the fight and tried to leave. However, the authorities arrived and attempted to apprehend Hulk. Feeling sorry for the gamma-spawned monster, the Surfer rescued him. However, Hulk still sought to find safety on another world and tried to take the Surfer's board. The Surfer refused to help him and, after a brief clash, the Surfer attempted to read Hulk's mind and learned Hulk's origins. When the Surfer tried to cure Hulk, the monster awoke, thought he was trying to attack him and fought him off. Having become fed up, the Surfer condemned Hulk to his curse and left.[198]

Roaming around in the wilderness, Hulk was discovered by men working for the High Evolutionary. Knocking Hulk out with specially made pellets, Hulk was then loaded into a ship that blasted off for the Evolutionary's planet, Wundagore II, where his New Men were currently in revolt.
