En route Hulk revived and attacked the ship's pilot, Sir Ram, before realizing he was in outer space.[199] As the ship neared Wundagore II, Sir Ram revived and realized they were heading into a deadly cosmic storm. The ship made it through and, while Sir Ram died of radiation poisoning, Hulk was restored to human form. Arriving on the planet, Banner was informed on what was happening, and the High Evolutionary immobilized Banner with his vacuum ray and then placed him in a device, intending to enhance his evolution by millions of years.[200] However, the process was interrupted when the New Men attacked the High Evolutionary's base, forcing the High Evolutionary to release Banner and fight back. During the attack, Banner turned into the Hulk one more and fought against the New Men. Gravely injured, the High Evolutionary was forced to use his device on himself, transforming himself into a godlike being. Before joining with the Universal Consciousness, the High Evolutionary reverted his New Men into their base evolutionary forms and then returned Hulk to Earth.[201]

Back on Earth, Hulk began trying to find a place to live in peace. While bounding across the wilderness, he knocked a plane out of the sky. It was piloted by a spy for the Lords of the Living Lightning. Rescued from the crash, the spy convinced Hulk to accompany him to the Lords' headquarters. There, their leader, Lightning Lord, convinced Hulk that they sought peace and, after capturing Talbot, further convinced Hulk to attack a military missile base.[202] While Hulk attacked the military base, keeping Ross and his soldiers busy, the Lords of the Living Lightning took over the facility. Hulk was knocked out by a powerful sedative gas during the battle and locked up in a cell with Betty, as Lightning Lord assumed that Hulk would harm the girl, thus pressuring Ross to surrender the base.[203] However, Lightning Lord's plan began to fall apart when Hulk refused to harm Betty and attacked him. When Lightning Lord fought back, his lightning weapon triggered Hulk's transformation back into Banner. The military began retaking the base, forcing the Lords of the Living Lightning to flee back to their base, where they planned to launch missiles at the base. With time running out, Banner convinced Ross to allow himself to use his gamma ray projector to force another transformation into the Hulk. Transformed again, Hulk then rushed to the Lords' base and attacked, destroying their atomic pile and causing a massive explosion that destroyed their base.[204]

Hulk survived, and while Namor the Sub-Mariner sought an alliance with Hulk, the Puppet Master used his radioactive clay to take control of Hulk. Under the Puppet Master's control, Hulk freed himself from the rubble of the Lords' base. When he was approached by Rick, Hulk was ordered to attack anyone who came near and he struck down his staunchest ally. As Hulk bounded away, Ross and Talbot vowed to destroy Hulk no matter what. Hulk was then lured to Namor along the Miami coast. When Namor offered a partnership, Hulk was forced to attack. The two fought across the beaches of Florida, but no matter how hard the Puppet Master pushed, Hulk could not be made to kill Namor. Namor was able to defeat Hulk by making a massive tidal wave that sent Hulk crashing on a nearby island where he reverted back into Banner; the tidal wave also destroyed the Puppet Master's base. Not recognizing Banner, Namor returned to the ocean with no further incident.[205]

Banner came under to the attention of Loki, who once more sought to manipulate Hulk to his own ends. This time, Loki transformed Banner back into Hulk and transported him to Asgard. There, Hulk bested Heimdall, the guardian at the gates of the golden realm. Breaching the gates of Asgard, Hulk clashed with the Warriors Three. Hulk soon lost the urge to fight and the Warriors determined Hulk to have been manipulated. Seeking to find out who transported Hulk to Asgard, the Warriors Three suggested they seek the advice of Oldar the Oracle. When they attempted to cross a bottomless pit, Loki struck Hulk with another mystical bolt, causing him to revert back into Banner and fall into the chasm.[206]

Banner was saved by sudden death by Amora the Enchantress, who sought to learn what she could about the whereabouts of Hercules, whom she was smitten by. She and Skurge the Executioner had aligned themselves with the trolls that lived beneath Asgard for a planned invasion. Banner was questioned about Hercules, but when Banner had no information, Amora ordered Skurge to kill him. Banner transformed into the Hulk again and fought off the two Asgardians and their troll army. When a cave-in separated them, Amora led her forces to attack. Hulk followed after them, then fought off the trolls and forced them to retreat. Gravely wounded by Amora, Hulk was restored to health by Asgard's ruler Odin. Seeing Odin's Sceptre of Power and thinking that he was being attacked, he was stopped by the Warriors Three, who convinced Odin that Hulk was not in control of his actions, staying the ruler's wrath. However, Odin still banished Hulk back to Earth.[207]

Rampage in New York[]

Hulk was teleported right in the center of Times Square in New York, where he immediately went on a rampage and then fled to the rooftops from the authorities. There, he reverted back into Banner; stealing some clothes, Banner managed to sneak across the city to the apartment owned by Rick and convinced the landlord to let him in. With Rick away, Banner turned on the television, where he was horrified to find a interview with Ross, Talbot and Rick. During the interview, Rick admitted that he considered Hulk a threat and one that should be destroyed. Just then, Rick returned to his apartment and tried to hold Banner at gunpoint. When they were interrupted by Betty, Rick lost his nerve and shot the floor instead of Banner. Unknown to them at the time, Banner was being observed by the Space Parasite, who sought to battle Hulk and drain his life energies. In order to trigger a transformation, the Space Parasite used a device that altered Betty's mood to make her lash out at Banner, triggering a transformation into the Hulk. The Space Parasite then teleported into the room and fought Hulk. Their fight took them into Yankee Stadium. Although the Space Parasite managed to drain some of Hulk's life energy, Hulk proved to be too powerful a foe, and the Space Parasite was beaten to the point where he was near death. When Hulk refused to kill him, the Space Parasite fled to space to die there. In the aftermath of the battle, Hulk was doused with tear gas by the police, which triggered another transformation back to human form and Banner was arrested.[208]

Banner was taken into military custody and was kept sedated while they transported him to JFK International Airport to be taken to a military facility. Along the way, the convoy was attacked by the Rhino, who was sent by his employers to capture Banner. While the Rhino nearly succeeded in capturing both Banner and Betty, the plan ultimately failed when Banner transformed into the Hulk once again. Getting Betty to safety, Hulk then battled the Rhino one-on-one. During the course of the battle, when Hulk made a fuel tanker explode on Rhino. Seeing the military come to Betty's aid, Hulk assumed that she was still in danger, so he grabbed her and bounded off.[209] Betty convinced Hulk to return her to her hotel room so she could get clothes to wear, but when she tried to enter, she ran into a pair of car thieves. Hulk came to Betty's rescue, but he suddenly transformed back into Banner and was shot in the leg while the thieves fled. The gunshots attracted the police and Betty tried to escape with Banner in her own car. When the authorities started to shoot at them, Banner bailed out of the car, transforming into the Hulk once again. Hulk then proceeded to go on a rampage through the city.[210]

Hulk continued to flee the authorities across the city and eventually crossed paths with the Missing Link, a mutated and radioactive caveman that was unleashed upon New York by Communist agents. During their first clash, the Missing Link's radiation caused another transformation of Hulk's body back into Banner, but still retaining Hulk's mind. This proved to be short-lived, as Hulk returned to his normal form while pursuing the Missing Link. As Hulk fought the Missing Link, Talbot and Rick arrived on the scene with a device created by Mr. Fantastic that was intended to restore Banner to normal permanently. When Hulk seemingly destroyed the Missing Link, Talbot blasted him with the device, changing him back into Banner just as the Missing Link freed itself from the rubble.[210]

Banner got Talbot and Rick to flee the scene, while he was injured and stayed behind. When the Missing Link grabbed him, his radioactive body caused him to change back into Hulk once again. The two fought it out while the authorities arrived.[211] Hulk was briefly separated from the Missing Link and was chased by the authorities, then Hulk also crossed paths with Captain America and the two fought. A guilt-stricken Rick tried to come to Hulk's aid and get everyone to stand down. This time, Rick's luck ran out on him, as falling debris from compromised buildings injured him seriously. Frustrated by his attackers, Hulk left, abandoning his staunchest supporter.[212] By the time Hulk found and resumed his battle with the Missing Link, Ross had called for S.H.I.E.L.D. to intervene; however, Hulk and the Missing Link were actually recovered by a Russian-owned Helicarrier commanded by Russian agent Yuri Brevlov and taken back to Russia before Nick Fury and his S.H.I.E.L.D. agents could arrive.[211] During this battle, Rick was injured by Hulk and then taken in by Captain America to become the new Bucky.[212]

Trapped in Asia[]

Hulk and the Missing Link were flown into Russian airspace; there, Hulk broke free from his cell and started trashing the Russian Helicarrier, eventually getting free. Yuri and his soldiers were forced to follow Hulk in a smaller ship when the Missing Link's radioactive body hit critical mass and exploded, destroying both the Helicarrier and seemingly the Missing Link himself. They tracked down Hulk, who had come to the aid of a small boy who was caught in the middle of their battle.[211] The Russian soldiers were prevented from attacking Hulk further thanks to the intervention of S.H.I.E.L.D., who incapacitated their ship. Hulk fled to a nearby village where he turned the child over to the villagers, who then attacked him. The boy pleaded in Hulk's case and Hulk was allowed to leave. As Hulk left, he was teleported to the secret Gobi Desert base of the Mandarin, who sought to use Hulk to trigger World War III in the hopes of taking over the world and rebuilding it to suit his feudalist ideals. The Mandarin tested Hulk's abilities and was suitably impressed, but when he asked Hulk to join him, the angered brute attacked, tearing a path of destruction through the Mandarin's headquarters until the Mandarin managed to trap him in a pit of quicksand.[213]

Hulk managed to free himself, only to be trapped in a glass cylinder and gassed. This allowed the Mandarin to place a mind control device on the back of Hulk's neck. Hulk was then sent out to the Chinese province of Tsen-Tse, where he clashed with the Chinese military. Hulk's mindless attack was stopped thanks to the interference of Nick Fury and Yuri Brevlov, who tracked down the Mandarin and destroyed his mind control device. Furious at being manipulated, Hulk leaped back to the Mandarin's Gobi Desert base and trashed it, causing it to collapse into rubble, but the Mandarin managed to escape.[214] While climbing the mountains of the region, Hulk scared some locals who went after him. As he was trying to get away, he crossed paths with the huge Inhuman dog Lockjaw, whom Hulk assumed was part of the attacking party. Fighting Lockjaw, Hulk was teleported to another dimension and placed into a prison that held all of the members of the League of Evil Inhumans: Leonus, Timberius, Aireo, Falcona, Nebulo, and Stallior.[215]

These Inhumans watched in awe as Hulk was able to smash through the energy barrier that kept them imprisoned. Freed, they were confronted by the League's leader Maximus the Mad, who convinced Hulk to join his cause to usurp the throne of the Great Refuge. Hulk was convinced and assisted Maximus and the others in getting into a chamber, where a deadly energy source had been locked away since it was invented by an ancient Inhuman scientist Romnar. Hulk's great strength proved to be the key to smashing through the barrier, allowing Maximus to get a hold of the energy and use it to threaten to destroy the Inhuman kingdom unless his brother Black Bolt surrendered the throne. However, Maximus' allies tried to betray him and use his weapon to destroy Hulk. While Black Bolt forced Maximus to cut off the source of the weapon's power, Hulk clashed with the League of Evil Inhumans and defeated them all in combat. When Black Bolt went to confront Hulk, the pair exchanged blows until Nebulo attempted to use the weapon on Black Bolt. Hulk disarmed Nebulo, but was engulfed in the deadly energy. Black Bolt then saved Hulk's life and, realizing that Hulk was an unwitting pawn of the entire ordeal, offered him a chance to live among the Inhumans. Seeing that every Inhuman except for Black Bolt feared him, Hulk declined the offer and left in peace, hoping to find a place where everyone could accept him for what he was.[215]

Galaxy Master[]

Hulk continued to travel through Asia even as Earth's axis began to shift in an unnatural fashion, causing freak weather patterns all over the world. Fighting his way onto a Chinese rocket test site, Hulk mistook a missile for a rocket leaving Earth and tried to ride upon it. The missile was launched and exploded in Antarctica, sending Hulk crashing into the prehistoric realm known as the Savage Land, where he reverted back into Banner. Banner was found by the Swamp Men, who sought to sacrifice him to their god, Umbu the Unliving. Banner was rescued from the Swamp Men by Ka-Zar and his saber-toothed cat, Zabu.[216]

Upon learning that Banner was a scientist, Ka-Zar brought him to a nearby cave where a strange device was running. Examining it, Banner was horrified to learn that it was causing Earth's axis to shift. Before Banner could disable the device, the Swamp Men attacked again, triggering another transformation into Hulk. Hulk frightened off the Swamp Men, and when Ka-Zar tried to reason with Hulk to disable the device, the brute swatted Ka-Zar away, knocking him out.[216] As Hulk battled with Ka-Zar and Zabu, the effigy of Umbu — a giant robot left by the alien Sagittarians for their ruler, the Galaxy Master — came to life and began heading toward the machine in the cave. Umbu crossed paths with Hulk and a battle began, but Hulk was felled by gas that caused him to revert back into Banner. No longer detecting Hulk, Umbu continued on his course. Banner then rushed to the cave and managed to deactivate the device, which also deactivated Umbu. But the deadly radiation from the device seemingly killed him, and his body was found by Ka-Zar.[217]

Detecting that Umbu and their doomsday device to destroy Earth were both deactivated, the Sagittarians sent a Titan Time-Probe to recover the one that was responsible for the deed so that they could deliver him to their ruler, the Galaxy Master, for revenge. Banner's dead body was recovered from the Savage Land, and the Sagittarians used their advanced science on their starship to resurrect Banner in the hopes of exacting revenge. After scanning his mind and learning nothing of any value, the Galaxy Master ordered Banner ejected out of the ship's airlock. Just over the orbit of the planet Sagittarius, Banner transformed into Hulk again as the airlock opened. The powerful brute was able to survive in the vacuum of outer space long enough to cause heavy damage to the Sagittarians' starship, causing it to crash-land on their homeworld. Recovering from the crash, Hulk was confronted by the energy form of the Galaxy Master, who was bent on destroying the beast that had ruined his plans for universal domination.[218]

As Hulk battled Galaxy Master and his ever-changing forms, his battle inspired Princess Daydra and her rebel forces to also attack the Galaxy Master in order to free themselves from his tyranny. When Galaxy Master turned into a suffocating gas, Hulk was knocked out, prompting the rebels to attack. Galaxy Master made short work of the rebels and then tried to draw the Princess into his body. Reviving, Hulk jumped into the tractor beam and was drawn into Galaxy Master's energy form instead. With Hulk inside his energy matrix, Galaxy Master was defenceless against Hulk's attack. When Hulk destroyed the nucleolus within the Galaxy Master, his threat was seemingly eliminated. In thanks, Daydra provided Hulk with a ship to return him home. However, Hulk was impatient and left before the pressure inside the ship could be properly calibrated. Although Hulk was able to survive within, he changed back into Banner, whose body was not conditioned to survive within the craft and was at risk of being crushed to death.[219]

Many Unhappy Returns[]

Clinging to life, Banner managed to save himself when he found that the ship that he was in was powered by gamma radiation. Unleashing the energy source triggered another transformation into Hulk, saving his life when the ship crash-landed on Earth. Recovering from the crash, Hulk was confronted by the Sandman, who sought Hulk's alliance so he could obtain the military's new space-warp ship in the hopes that he could reunite with his ally from the Negative Zone, Blastaar the Living Bomb-Burst, in order to get revenge on the Fantastic Four. At first, Hulk fought back, but then he was tricked into attacking the base. But, when Hulk arrived, he remembered that Betty often spent time there and held back until the soldiers attacked him, spurring him into a violent rage. Hulk fought the Army until he spotted the Sandman trying to escape with the space-warp ship and about to ram into a car with Betty inside. Hulk slammed the Sandman's transport out of the way and the two began to fight. Hulk ultimately won the bout by sweeping the Sandman's particles off the base and then fled the base when Ross tried to congratulate him, thinking it was another attack.[220]

Growing tired, Hulk reverted back to Banner, who was now more determined than ever to find a cure for himself and went seeking out Betty, hoping that she could help him. Banner found Betty sequestered to a room on base, but their romantic reunion was cut short when Banner was caught in the room by Talbot, who raised the alarm. The advancing soldiers excited Banner enough to trigger another change into Hulk, who tried to escape with Betty. Outside the base, both were attacked by the Mandarin and the Sandman, who had just recently teamed up to defeat Hulk. Gassing Hulk and Betty, the two villains captured both of them and spirited them away to one of the Mandarin's nearby secret hideouts. When Hulk recovered from the gas, he found himself pinned to a metal table with energy beams that fed off his own gargantuan strength. But, like many other traps that had held him before, this was only a temporary setback, as Hulk gained the strength to break free once he saw that Betty was in danger. Hulk fought both the Mandarin and the Sandman until they threatened to toss Betty into a massive pressure cooker. Hulk, however, still fought back. Seeing that his plan was a failure, the Mandarin knocked the Sandman into the pressure cooker with a blast from one of his rings and fled. The Sandman was transformed into living glass, but before Hulk could shatter him, Betty convinced Hulk not to kill him. While Hulk's guard was down, he was blasted from behind by soldiers led by Talbot, who were armed with a neutralization ray. As Hulk began to pass out, he accused Betty of betraying him before blacking out and being taken into custody.[221]

With Hulk now in the military's possession and sedated by the neutralization ray, his arch-enemy the Leader chose that moment to reveal that he had survived his last encounter with Hulk. He then offered the military a means of containing Hulk indefinitely under the auspices that he was attempting to undo his past wrongs, but was secretly plotting to gain control of the military installation in order to trigger World War III and take over whatever was left of the world. After a failed attempt to escape, Hulk was then trapped in a massive Plasti-Thene prison constructed by the Leader that could withstand Hulk's repeated blows, a seemingly impenetrable prison.[222] Ultimately, Betty overheard the Leader's plot to take over the world and, while unable to convince her father of this, convinced Talbot that their only means of stopping the Leader and his huge Super-Humanoid was to free Hulk. Unable to get Hulk to cooperate, Talbot tried to get the soldiers on base to subdue the Leader, but he incapacitated all the troops with his mental powers. Alone, Betty was able to use the Leader's devices to free Hulk from his prison. When Hulk fought back, the Leader used a gun that created another miniature Plastithene prison closely around Hulk's body and then prepared a nuclear warhead for launch.[223]

Hulk managed to break free of this prison also, but when he resumed his battle, the Leader teleported Hulk and his Super-Humanoid to a nearby island to prevent the Jade Giant from thwarting his missile launch. Hulk destroyed the Super-Humanoid by tossing it into a nearby volcano, but returned to the base too late to stop the Leader from launching the nuclear missile. As the Leader fled for cover in a bomb shelter, Betty managed to calm Hulk enough to make him revert to Banner. Banner then recalled a hunter missile that he had constructed and then used it to intercept the nuclear missile, blowing it out of the sky. The pressure triggered another transformation into Hulk, who went looking for the Leader, catching him moments after he launched a second nuclear miisile. This time, Hulk was able to leap up and redirect the missile high into the air, where it exploded harmlessly. Seeing his plan had failed, the Leader fled, passing by the unconscious body of Banner as he fell into the ocean below but ignoring the significance of what was floating there so as to make his escape.[224]

Banner was recovered by the Atlantean royal Lady Dorma, who gave Banner a potion that would allow him to breathe underwater and took him to Atlantis to recover from his injuries. When Mistress Fara, a rival for Namor's affections, saw Dorma secreting Banner into her room, she went to Namor and convinced him that his lover was betraying him with a surface dweller. When Namor went to confront Lady Dorma, an argument ensued while Banner awakened. Confused and excited, Banner transformed into Hulk once again and he attacked Namor. The two battled across Atlantis causing much damage, which cost Mistress Fara her life. Hulk did not fare any better battling Namor this time either, as he proved no match for the Atlantean prince in his natural element. Knocked to shore by a massive tidal wave, Hulk reverted back into Banner. Once again, when Namor went looking for his foe and found only Banner, he returned to the ocean — still not making the connection between the two of them.[225]

Banner awakened to find himself in the Central American nation of Costa Salvador. Looking around, he found that everyone was in a trance-like state thanks to a massive robot construct that projected strange beams of energy. Finding one lone native who was not under its control, Banner learned that the island was under the control of "the Great One". Finding himself falling under the influence of the beams, Banner tried to fight their effects, triggering a transformation into Hulk, who was immune to the beams' control. Hulk then leapt to the castle of the "Great One" and discovered that it was the hideout of Maximus and the League of Evil Inhumans. Hulk fought off the League of Evil Inhumans until the United States Air Force, coming to the aid of Costa Salvador due to a mutual protection agreement, arrived. Hulk found himself confused as to who to fight: Maximus and his legions, or the military who had both hunted and hounded him for so many years.[226] Maximus managed to convince Hulk to fight off the military, unaware that Betty had stowed away on her father's plane. Upon discovering this and learning that Maximus intended to kill the invaders, Hulk turned on him. Maximus, in turn, unleashed his mind control robot, which Hulk easily destroyed. As Maximus and his forces fled in a ship, the military once more attempted to apprehend Hulk but, not wishing to be imprisoned again, Hulk easily leaped away to seek peace somewhere else.[227]

Hulk found himself in the Florida Everglades, where his large leaps inadvertently put him in the path of a missile test. Struck by the missile, Hulk crashed into the nearby swamp. Wading through the mire, Hulk unknowingly smashed through a United States Government radioactive waste disposal shed. The cracked barrels of waste seeped into the swamp, resurrecting the mortal remains of criminal Joe Timms as a swamp monster that was later named the Glob. The military managed to track down Hulk and attack him again. While Hulk defended himself, the Glob, meanwhile, kidnapped Betty and took her into the swamp. Eventually, Hulk crossed paths with the Glob and tried to free Betty from him. The battle ended when the Glob crossed back into the radioactive swamp water that spawned him and began to dissolve. The Glob's last action was to hold Betty above water, keeping her safe long enough for Hulk to recover her. Distressed by the Glob's sacrifice, Hulk left Betty for the military when they arrived and fled into the swamp to reflect on the entire encounter.[228]

No Happiness for Bruce Banner[]

Hulk went south where, in his confused mind, he thought an oncoming train was attacking him and derailed it. Fleeing into the wilderness, Hulk passed out and changed back into Banner. Banner then went down to survey the wreckage that he had caused and happened to come across a newspaper report stating that Mister Fantastic of the Fantastic Four had devised a cure for Hulk. Banner then hopped the next freight train heading into New York in the hopes of finally being cured. While riding the rails, Banner began working on a complimenting formula with the one designed by Reed Richards. The ride was cut short when two hoboes who were also riding in the freight car mistook Banner making a pouch for his formula as something valuable and tried to rob him. This triggered another, albeit brief, transformation into Hulk. Banner eventually made his way to New York City, but when he arrived at the Baxter Building, the headquarters at the Fantastic Four, the security guard on duty was unwilling to listen. Angered, Banner transformed into Hulk once again and forced his way up into the Fantastic Four's headquarters. As the Fantastic Four battled Hulk, Banner's formula came loose and was recovered by the Invisible Girl, who turned it over to Mister Fantastic. Using this formula, he calibrated a sonic blaster that was able to knock out Hulk, allowing them to begin the experiment that they all hoped would cure Banner of being Hulk once and for all.[229]

Thanks to Mister Fantastic, Banner gained the ability to transform into the Hulk at will while still maintaining his intelligence. Vowing to never become Hulk again, Banner proposed to Betty, who accepted.[230] Sadly, the Leader recruited the Rhino and fired a gamma gun during Banner and Betty's wedding, again causing Banner to turn into Hulk, but returning him to his savage state. Hulk clashed with the Rhino and the Leader, hospitalizing Ross and destroying his home. Hulk escaped, and Talbot vowed to Betty that he would destroy Hulk if Ross died.[231] Returning to the desert, Hulk was sought out by the X-Men, who were seeking one of Banner's inventions that could heal their injured leader, Professor X. Although they briefly clashed, Banner returned long enough to give the X-Men what they needed to save their leader.[232]

Banner agreed to work with Talbot to try and stop a radioactive comet that was threatening Earth. This "comet" turned out to actually be the Absorbing Man, whom Hulk defeated.[233] Banner was captured by a cult that sought to release their demonic masters, the Undying Ones. Hulk was sent into the realm of the Night-Crawler along with Barbara Norriss. Doctor Strange came to Hulk's aid to stop the Undying Ones. Barbara Norris sacrificed her life so that the two heroes could escape.[234] Hulk once again became a pawn in the ongoing feud between the Mole Man and Tyrannus. This time, Tyrannus attempted to win Hulk's cooperation by making him befriend his robot, Mogol. When Hulk learned that the creature was really a robot, he considered this a betrayal and destroyed it, leaving Tyrannus' realm.[235] Trying to get to the surface world, Hulk nearly caused a massive earthquake by affecting fault lines on the West Coast, leading to a clash with his former team, the Avengers.[236] Hulk was again targeted by the Leader, who revived the Glob and sent him after Hulk in a plot that ultimately ended in another failure for the Leader.[237]

Rick sought out his old friend to find a way to separate himself from the Kree soldier Captain Marvel, but a student protest set Banner off, leading to a clash with Captain Marvel.[238] Another former colleague, Dr. Raoul Stoddard, succeeded in splitting Hulk from Banner, sending Hulk on a rampage to destroy Banner.[239] Hulk fled the military, hid out in the slums of Los Angeles and befriended the young African American Jim Wilson while Banner, the military and Iron Man attempted to track down Hulk in order to re-merge Banner and Hulk.[240] After again merging Hulk with Banner, the military asked Jim to stay with them in order to keep Hulk under control. Jim was also targeted by the terrorist organization Hydra, who also sought to control Hulk. This plot ended in failure; however, Jim was seriously injured. Betty then suffered a nervous breakdown from the stress of dealing with Banner's double life as Hulk.[241]

Have Hulk, Will Travel[]

Hulk ended up in the nation of Morvania and helped the resistance remove its dictator, Václav Draxon.[242] Trapped in the future and seeking revenge against the Avengers, Kang the Conqueror sent Hulk back in time to World War I to kill the Phantom Eagle. Hulk foiled this plot and successfully returned to his own time.[54] Hulk and Abomination (the latter of whom had somehow escaped from the Stranger (how this happened is unknown)) were both enslaved by Xeron the Starslayer and traveled the stars to hunt down and kill the creature known as Klaatu.[243] Although Abomination attempted to kill Banner/Hulk, the crew's captain, Cybor, seemingly slew Klaatu. Hulk and Abomination clashed, sending them both crashing back to Earth.[244] Hulk then clashed with the Sandman again, who tried to force a blood transfusion with Betty in order to stop himself from turning into glass, which was successful in changing the Sandman's body back to normal. The defeated Sandman was lost in a whirlpool, while Betty was transformed into a solid glass statue as a result of the blood transfusion.[245]

In the South American nation of San Diablo, Hulk and the Silver Surfer were recruited by Namor the Sub-Mariner into a group called the Titans Three to destroy a weather control device that threatened Earth.[246] This led to a clash with the Avengers until Namor's scientist, Ikthon, could repair a flaw in the device. Confused, Hulk fled the scene.[247] The Leader sought to exert Hulk to the point where the monster would die of a heart attack. He created psycho-projections of many of Hulk's enemies and used them to lead Hulk towards the hospital where Betty was, threatening to shatter Betty's fragile glass form into pieces if anyone tried to stop him. Thanks to interference from Jim Wilson, the Leader's plot was foiled.[248]

Hulk was captured by the military with aid from Mister Fantastic and Professor X; however, he was teleported away by the insectoid being named Psyklop. Psyklop sought to shrink Hulk down in size and use him as a power source to bring his masters, the Dark Gods, to Earth. The Avengers interrupted, causing Hulk to shrink out of sight[249] and get transported to the Microverse world of K'ai. On K'ai, the Banner persona was restored, and Hulk joined a rebellion led by Jarella against the evil warlord Visis. Hulk and Jarella formed a relationship, and they were prepared to wed when Psyklop found Hulk and brought him back to Earth. With his savage state restored, Psyklop's base was smashed, and Hulk escaped.[250] With only vague memories of his adventure on K'ai, Banner was taken back to the military when psychiatrist Leonard Samson came up with a dual solution for curing Banner and restoring Betty to human form. Samson was successful in this; however, he used the siphoned gamma radiation to mutate himself into a gamma-spawned Adonis whom he named Doc Samson. Doc Samson romanced Betty, making Banner so jealous that he purposely bombarded himself with gamma radiation and again became the Hulk to fight Doc Samson. When Betty vocalized concern for Doc Samson over Hulk, Hulk fled the scene.[251]

Hulk became the new pet project of the Parrington family. Hulk was targeted by Amora the Enchantress, who turned the Parringtons' daughter, Samantha, into a host for the Valkyrie to battle Hulk. The plot ended in failure and Samantha reverted to normal.[252] His next rampage through New York made Banner the subject of a military manhunt. He was rescued by Doctor Doom,[253] who smuggled Banner into Latveria in order to exploit his brilliant mind and then sent Hulk out with a bomb in order to annex neighboring countries into Latveria. This was opposed by Doom's childhood love, Valeria, and led to a battle between Doom and Hulk. Hulk fled when he realized that Valeria could have been harmed if the fight had continued.[254]

Doctor Strange recruited Hulk, Namor the Sub-Mariner, and the Silver Surfer to stop Yandroth from setting his Omegatron to destroy Earth. They formed a loose-knit "non-team" of heroes known as the Defenders. Hulk answered a call from the Avengers to help to stop Ares and Amora the Enchantress from fulfilling a prophecy that would have given Ares mastery over the entire world.[255] Hulk later ended up in Egypt, where he was talked into taking a part in a film being made there. Banner was fired from the film set and was caught in the middle of the Horusians' God-Spawn battle, destroying their champion, the Colossus.[256]

Project Greenskin[]

The U.S. military built Project Greenskin, a.k.a. Hulkbuster Base, as a specialized facility to capture and imprison Hulk. Upon its construction, Ross was replaced with a robot duplicate by the Leader. The Leader was disguised as Talbot in the hopes of not only destroying Hulk, but replacing both the President and the Vice President of the United States with robot duplicates as well.[257] Hulk foiled the Leader's plot and, in the aftermath of the battle, Doc Samson lost his gamma-spawned powers. Hulk fled into the desert, briefly encountering a mirage city that would vanish as quickly as it appeared.[258]

Hulk was again captured by the military and cured by Peter Corbeau. Jarella then transported herself to Earth to seek out Hulk. She was followed by an assassin that was sent by Visis. To save her, Banner re-exposed himself to gamma radiation and again became Hulk. When it was determined that Jarella's mere presence on Earth risked Earth's destruction, Jarella willingly returned to K'ai.[109] Sedated at Project Greenskin, Hulk battled the High Evolutionary's exiled New Man, the Inheritor, when the creature came seeking out radiation to prolong its evolved state.[259] When Hulk came across Lorna Dane, he confused her for Jarella and captured her. Lorna was saved by her fellow X-Man, Havok. Betty heard Banner calling out for Jarella, prompting her to begin a romance with Talbot.[260]

Banner sought out Hank Pym in Washington, D.C. to find a means to shrink small enough to return to Jarella's world. There, Banner learned that Pym's talk had been cancelled; this enraged him so much that he transformed into the Hulk, who went on a rampage. Hulk ultimately saved Washington, D.C. from Senator Morton Clegstead who, while trying to find a cure for cancer via gamma radiation, had mutated into a massive pile of ooze.[261] Returning to the Nevada desert, Hulk was captured by Project Greenskin and S.H.I.E.L.D. Banner was put on trial for Hulk's rampage in Washington, D.C. Lawyer Matt Murdock (alias Daredevil) represented Banner.[262] It seemed likely that Hulk would be sentenced to death until Reed Richards offered to try and cure Banner with his Nega-Gamma Gun; however, this only strengthened Hulk further, allowing him to escape.[263]

Hulk broke into Pym's lab and drank one of his shrinking formulas. This caused him to shrink to miniature size, and he was captured by the Chameleon, who was then working for Hydra. Hulk attempted to escape Hydra's clutches with the help of Ant-Man; however. the unstable formula shrank him down into the Microverse.[264] As he shrank down in size, he ruined the fantasy world that was created by the Shaper of Worlds for the former Nazi Otto Kronsteig.[265] Finally reaching Jarella's world, Hulk, with Banner's intellect restored, again helped Jarella overthrow Visis. Pym's formula then wore off, both causing Hulk to grow back to his normal size and sending him back to Earth.[266]

Defenders[]

Hulk was reunited with his fellow Defenders to fight the Dread Dormammu in Rutland, Vermont,[267] to stop Xemnu the Living Titan's attempt to change Earth's children into members of his long-dead race,[268] and lastly to foil a plot by the evil Necrodamus, who was attempting to sacrifice Hulk's friend, Namor the Sub-Mariner.[80] Hulk was reunited with Jim Wilson, after which he learned of Betty's upcoming marriage to Talbot. He was then forced to battle a Leader-controlled Rhino.[269] Rhino and Hulk were launched into outer space by the Leader and ended up on the High Evolutionary's Counter-Earth, where they were embroiled in a battle between the New Men. During this adventure Hulk met Counter-Earth's version of Bruce Banner, who was married to Betty Ross and had a son, Bruce Jr. The conflict ended with Hulk and the Rhino being shot back to Earth-616.[270] With the Leader's shuttle with Hulk and the Rhino aboard blasted out of the sky while it returned to Earth, Ross forced Abomination to go out and keep Hulk both busy and away from Betty and Talbot's wedding. Abomination lost the fight, but he did succeed in his task. Learning that Betty was heading to Niagara Falls, he went after her.[271]

Hulk got sidetracked when he was recruited by Doctor Strange to rejoin the Defenders in searching for the Silver Surfer, clashing with Calizuma.[272] The group ended up in the realm of the Undying Ones, battling their leader the Nameless One and rescuing Barbara Norris.[273] They next clashed with Amora the Enchantress and Skurge the Executioner, ending with Barbara being revived as another host for the Valkyrie.[274] The Defenders were then called to clash with the Omegatron which, with the aid of the Valkyrie, they destroyed.[275]

From that point on, both during and after his time with the Defenders as well as all alone, Hulk continued to be hunted by the U.S. military and battled many enemies both old and new including, among others, a second fight between himself and Xemnu the Living Titan and before that, five separate fights between himself and Xemnu's duplicates of the deadliest of several alien monsters that visited Earth in the past: Diablo the Demon from the Fifth Dimension, Taboo the Thing from the Murky Swamp, Groot the Monster from Planet X, Goom the Thing from Planet X, and the Blip.[276]

The Birth of She-Hulk[]

One day Banner went to visit his beloved cousin, Jennifer Walters, who had become a Los Angeles-based lawyer. At that time, Walters had been defending a hood named Lou Monkton, whom a gangster named Nicholas Trask had framed for murder. While Walters drove Banner to her home, one of Trask's henchmen shot her. To save his cousin's life, Banner improvised an emergency blood transfusion. Walters died but, thanks to the transfusion, she was thrown into the Below-Place, where she was able to enter the metaphysical Green Door and return to life.[277] The transfusion of Banner's blood also mutated Walters, causing her to become the She-Hulk.[107]

One Mind, Two Bodies[]

After receiving two huge doses of gamma radiation, the first during a fight against both the Galaxy Master and the Abomination,[278] and another when being sent back to Earth from Halfworld,[279] Banner found that he remembered the events of the previous adventures in detail as opposed to the dreamlike quality that he normally had. During an encounter with the Wendigo, where he did not turn into Hulk despite the life-threatening situation, Banner determined that he could change at will and, after doing so, found that his mind was still in control. This realization led to him using Hulk's strength to help various groups across Canada and the U.S. and led to him receiving a Presidential pardon.[280] This change led to problems when encountering many of his old enemies, as his intelligence would override his rage, and Hulk would be out-muscled on more than one occasion.[281] The Savage Hulk personality began to reassert control after Banner was continuously assaulted by dreams sent by the demon Nightmare[282] who wanted to use Hulk in an attack against Doctor Strange. This influence was broken by Doctor Strange, but Banner transformed into the Hulk in his mind, destroyed Nightmare's realm, the Dream Dimension, and committed psychic suicide, leaving a near-mindless version of Savage Hulk as the sole occupant of the once-shared body.[283]

Hulk, along with a group of other super-heroes, was teleported to Battleworld by the Beyonder.[284]

Separated from the Hulk[]

Doc Samson captured Hulk[285] and succeeded in separating Banner's psyche and atomic structure from the larger atomic structure of the Hulk. Hulk's body, with all personality and memory removed, was inert until Samson stimulated the brain within the body. This new incarnation of the Hulk escaped and became a greater menace than ever before.[286] Banner became leader of a new Hulkbusters task force, which he headed from Gamma Base.[287] Banner finally married Betty, believing himself to be free of the curse of the Hulk.[288] During the honeymoon, Banner became gravely ill and was hospitalized.[289] Due to his separation from the Hulk, Banner's body began to lose molecular cohesion. Hulk's body soon followed suit and he was defeated by the Avengers.[290] With the aid of the synthezoid known as the Vision, Banner was re-merged with the Hulk. The original Hulk persona assumed control of the body;[291] however, the reintegration was unstable, and an attempt to stabilize, and possibly cure, Banner in a nutrient tank resulted in Hulk returning to his original gray incarnation who only manifested at sunset.

Rick absorbed the excess gamma radiation and became a light green-skinned Hulk-like creature when he was pushed into the nutrient bath by Ross, who was attempting to both sabotage the experiment and kill Hulk.[292] Banner reasoned that the best way to cure Rick was to use the machine from the Hulk's Cave to change himself into Hulk. Little did he know that this was a subliminal suggestion placed by Hulk himself who, once he was free, smashed the machine to avoid turning back into Banner. Complicating matters, the Leader arrived, having followed Hulk in the hopes of regaining his faded intellect. When he found the machine destroyed, the Leader made a deal with the now-smarter Hulk to transfer Rick's gamma radiation into himself. Shortly after, a dishonored Ross managed to take control of the electrical energy creature Zzzax. Ross and Rick were both defeated and the radiation energy was transferred from Rick to Sterns, which caused an explosion in the lab that led to the Leader's apparent death.[293]

Ground Zero[]

Little did either Hulk or Banner know that the Leader had survived and sent the vampiric Half-Life after him. Hulk tore off Half-Life's limbs close to sunrise before the villain could pull himself together.[294] The S.H.I.E.L.D. Council decided that they had enough Gamma Bombs so that Banner was no longer required and ordered Agent Clay Quartermain to murder him. The mutant bounty hunters X-Factor managed to locate Hulk and freeze him in place before placing a call to S.H.I.E.L.D. After transporting Hulk back to Gamma Base, Quartermain went against the orders of the Council before blowing up several large explosive charges that wiped out Gamma Base. Quartermain took Banner and Rick away from S.H.I.E.L.D. While on the way to the government stash of Gamma Bombs, Betty was released from the Leader's captivity to help stall them. She revealed that she was pregnant with Banner's child. Hulk decided to keep Betty safe, despite her being Banner's wife, not his. The quartet made their way to the government facility, but they found out - too late - that the Leader's two superhuman henchmen, Rock and Redeemer, had already taken a Gamma Bomb. When the Leader detonated it in Middletown with Hulk at ground zero, Hulk was assumed to be dead.[295]

In reality, Hulk had been transported to Jarella's Microverse world of K'ai moments before the detonation. There Hulk, now a deity to the K'aitians, helped a group of minor wizards to overthrow the "Grand Inquisitor" in return for a spell which was promised to rid him of Banner for good.[296]

Joe Fixit[]

When Hulk returned to Earth, he took a job as an enforcer at a Las Vegas casino. Calling himself Mr. Joe Fixit, Hulk spent several months without reverting to human form. It was during this time that he met and dated Marlo Chandler, who would one day marry Rick. Banner eventually returned and Hulk's life as Joe Fixit soon came to an end through the machinations of the Maggia.[297]

Multiple Personas[]

Banner found Betty working in a convent as a nun when he was attacked by Prometheus, an agent of a team called the Pantheon. The stress and anger of being unable to get to Betty caused Savage Hulk persona to resurface and sent Banner's psyche into turmoil. Gray Hulk managed to keep Savage Hulk behind a mental door, but he knew that, since he had been unleashed once, it was only a matter of time before Savage Hulk would take over.[298] When Hulk was needed to fight the Super-Skrull, Gray Hulk convinced Banner to bring him out instead of Savage Hulk. Gray Hulk managed to outsmart the Super-Skrull and managed to save Betty. Inside Banner's mind, Gray Hulk and Savage Hulk were fighting each other for dominance. Through hypnosis that was done with the help of the Ringmaster, Doc Samson created the green-skinned intelligent "Merged" Hulk - an integration of Banner's three separate personalities.[22]

The Pantheon[]

This incarnation of the Hulk joined the Pantheon. The Pantheon were led by Agamemnon, an immortal hybrid offspring of a human and an Asgardian. Unknown at the time was that, centuries earlier, Agamemnon had offered any of his offspring to the alien Troyjans in exchange for the ability to pass his godhood down to his descendants.[299] As a favor to their friend, Jim Wilson, Hulk and Rick agreed to help out at an AIDS benefit concert with Rick headlining and Hulk providing security. The concert was disrupted by the drug-addicted assassin Speedfreek, who was sent to kill one of the concert attendees. Jim was stabbed defending the man, and Hulk got rid of Speedfreek before he could kill anyone.[300]

During one of his missions with the Pantheon, Hulk fought alongside a rebel force in Trans-Sabal against both S.H.I.E.L.D.-issued Mandroids and the government mutant team X-Factor. Tran-Sabal's dictator, Farnoq Dahn, had promised the U.S. government energy assistance if they helped him keep his place as unchallenged ruler. He was exposed as a psychopath when he tried to win the war by tying a mother and child to two separate missiles and threatened to launch them if the Pantheon did not withdraw. Hulk and X-Factor, working together, stopped him. The tyrant was forced to face his people for the crimes he had committed, but most of them still saw him as a god and bowed at his feet. He was then shot and killed by a traumatized Rick.[301] Pantheon member Atalanta was shot down in the Himalayas by the Troyjan warrior Trauma, so Hulk, Ulysses, and Hector were sent to find her. Trauma found Atalanta and confessed his love to her before Hulk showed up and brought down an avalanche on top of him.[302]

During this time, Marlo was killed by a woman posing as Rick's mother. Because the Leader shared a mental bond with Rick, he offered to bring her back to life. The Leader attacked the Pantheon's headquarters, the Mount, using both his gamma soldiers and the U-Foes to distract Hulk so that he could ask Agamemnon for help against Hydra. Agamemnon agreed to help, and Hulk left in a rage. Agamemnon betrayed the Leader by sending Hulk to his hidden Arctic sanctuary of Freehold in order to kill him. Hulk crashed into Freehold during the middle of the Hydra invasion and when the Leader was trying to resurrect Marlo from the dead. Overcome with anger, Hulk ignored Rick's pleas to stop and destroyed the machine because he thought that the Leader was lying and taking advantage of his grieving friend. The Leader was seemingly killed in the battle. Hulk knocked the helmet off Redeemer, saw the resurrected Ross, and realized his mistake.[303]

When Agamemnon felt that it was time to venture out into the world to reconnect with the common people, he appointed Hulk as his replacement. On his first mission as leader, he traveled to the Amazon jungle to investigate a new company that was cutting down the rainforest. There, he was jumped by the Juggernaut, who was working as an enforcer for the New World Order (N.W.O.) and its leader, the Red Skull. Hulk was captured and brainwashed into fighting the Avengers, believing that the Juggernaut was Banner's own abusive father, Brian. Hulk was able to shake off the mind control when the Juggernaut praised him and he realized that Banner's real father would never have shown such kindness. The psychic backlash released the patchwork creature Piecemeal from his holding container.[304]

Hulk began showing signs of instability when he began referring to himself as "Hulk" or "Hulk" instead of "Bruce." As a favor to a former Pantheon member, Perseus, Hulk traveled to Loch Ness to investigate reports of a monster in the lake, which turned out to be Piecemeal. Hulk was about to defeat him when the Madman interfered. After Perseus was killed, Hulk killed Piecemeal and appeared to kill the Madman, but his body was never found. Using his new power as leader of the Pantheon, Hulk led a strike against a maximum security prison to free an ex-girlfriend who had been falsely imprisoned.[305] Trauma returned and kidnapped Atalanta in order to make her his bride. With the help of the Silver Surfer and the Starjammers, Hulk and the Pantheon attacked the Troyjans' homeworld. Upon arriving, they were all shocked when Trauma's father, the Troyjans' leader Lord Arm'Cheddon, told them the truth about Agamemnon. If they tried to take Atalanta back, then the Troyjans would take back the extended lives of the entire Pantheon. Hulk, not at all caring about the deal, attacked Trauma, and accidentally impaled him on his own shoulder spike. With his last words, Trauma pardoned the Pantheon and asked his father to let them all leave in peace.[306]

Maestro[]

You don't know what lies ahead for you. I do. Listen to me, Bruce... they're going to take it all away. You're going to end up with nothing and no one. Why go back to that... when you can stay here and have everything?

—Maestro

Hulk was taken into a possible alternate future by Rick's granddaughter, Janis, to fight his future self, the Maestro. The Maestro was a tyrant who had killed all the heroes and villains on Earth and named himself emperor of the post-apocalyptic world. He had the intelligence of Banner and was twice as strong as Hulk, their first fight ending with the Maestro breaking Hulk's neck and keeping him prisoner for the next few days as his wound healed. After Hulk confirmed that he could not defeat his future self in a straight fight, Maestro was killed when Hulk sent him back in time to ground zero at the moment the Gamma Bomb that created him had gone off, having determined that only a ground zero nuclear blast would be enough to kill him. After killing Maestro, Hulk was sent back to the present, haunted by the thought of him losing control and becoming the Maestro.[307]

Soon after this, Rick and Marlo were married. At the wedding, Betty told Hulk that she wanted to move into the Mount in order to be with him. After the wedding, Hulk was attacked by the disgraced Skrull warrior Talos the Untamed. In an effort to gain back some of his honor, Talos wanted to be killed by Earth's strongest warrior. Hulk refused to fight because of how well his relationship with Betty was going and he did not want to risk losing his temper again. Later, Hulk received news that his old friend, Jim Wilson, was at an AIDS protest that was getting out of control. He took him back to the Mount to give him treatment, but despite its advanced technology, Jim died.[308]

Trial of Agamemnon[]

Having discovered the truth about Agamemnon, Hulk and the rest of the Pantheon made him stand trial. Agamemnon resurrected all of the dead Pantheon warriors to kill everyone in the Mount. Agamemnon tried to escape, but he was instead killed by Atalanta, which brought an end to the undead warriors. Achilles, still loyal to Agamemnon, tried killing his teammate, Ulysses, but the bullet ricocheted and hit Betty. Hulk became so angry that he reverted to Banner's body with Hulk's brain, apparently the result of a psychic failsafe that he had created during the initial merging of his personas in order to prevent the return of Savage Hulk. Even in his human form he gave off enough gamma radiation to make Achilles vulnerable, and Ulysses killed him.[309]

First Death and Resurrection of Betty Banner[]

The Pantheon fled their former base, and the still-mindless Banner was taken into custody and temporarily placed in the care of Doc Samson while Betty was treated for the bullet wound. Nick Fury took Banner into S.H.I.E.L.D. custody because he was a fugitive. During Banner's transport Betty died, and her soul was given the chance to go to Heaven. First, she wanted to visit Banner to see if he still loved her. He calmed down when he saw her and was able to transform and escape. After seeing how important she was to him, Betty decided to live after all and returned to her body. Hulk visited the destroyed Mount and saw a hologram that had been set up by Paris, telling him that he was now the leader of the Pantheon and that Hulk had been fired from it.[310]

Living under the last name Danner, Hulk and Betty moved to Sunville, a small town in Florida. To hide his green skin, Hulk wore bandages all over his body and claimed to be a burn victim. Soon after their move, a child was killed by a gigantic shadowy figure, and Hulk was suspected of the crime because of his size. Upon investigation, Hulk found out that the true killer was a deranged old man living in the Florida Everglades with the Man-Thing, and rescued a child. A few days later, Hulk and Betty offered their help to a young and pregnant homeless girl. While they were at the clinic, protesters attacked and the girl was shot and killed. Hulk offered the girl's father his help in bringing her killer to justice. They learned that the killer was just a boy who had accidentally shot her when someone pushed him. The father revealed himself to be Speedfreek and tried to kill the boy. Hulk hurled a car battery at Speedfreek, which covered him in battery acid, burning most of the skin from his face and forcing him to flee.[311]

Hulk learned that the Abomination was fighting cops in the sewers of New York and decided that it was his problem. The homeless were being cleared out because the police commissioner was working for a drug lord who needed the sewers for new drug routes. While Hulk confronted Abomination, the cops used the opportunity to clear out the homeless by killing almost all of them. Abomination snapped and started killing all of the cops, then took his battle with Hulk to the surface. They crashed through the Daily Bugle Building before Abomination jumped onto a news helicopter and caused it to crash. He used the opportunity to escape while Hulk was distracted.[312]

Ghosts of the Future[]

An Army squad led by Matt Talbot, Glenn Talbot's nephew, captured Betty. After Hulk saw Talbot shoot Betty in both legs, he went so far over the edge that he reverted to his Banner form, and Banner was taken into custody. During a jailbreak, Banner, still with the mind of the Hulk, ran towards a grenade and nearly died when it went off. He was able to transform into the Hulk before he could be killed, but a shrapnel fragment was left in his brain, extremely hindering his intelligence.[313]

Seeking a device to remove the shrapnel in his brain, Hulk traveled to Freehold. With the Leader apparently dead, Freehold had been placed in the care of one of his followers, Omnibus. Omnibus believed that there would eventually be a nuclear war that would kill everyone on Earth, so he decided to speed it up by ordering terrorist attacks across the world to cause strain on global relations. He had also mentally controlled many high-ranking government officials, including Talbot, which explained his insane behavior. Jailbait overheard Omnibus' plan and exposed him to the people of Freehold, after which he was sentenced to death. Hulk decided that the best way to save the world would be to pose as the Maestro and claim to be the man behind the terrorist attacks. A psychotic Thor was sent to defeat him. It was a close battle until an atomic bomb was dropped on top of them. Hulk was believed dead by most of the world, but he had actually used a hidden Pantheon base to survive.[314]

Onslaught/Heroes Reborn[]

Traveling through Alaska, Hulk ran into Janis and took her to an unused Pantheon base; he was then mentally ordered by Onslaught to find and kill Cable. Cable and Storm were able to free Hulk from Onslaught's control, and they joined the rest of the heroes in New York for the battle against Onslaught. Hulk and Banner were separated after he destroyed Onslaught's body. Banner was among the heroes who sacrificed themselves to destroy Onslaught,[315] and Savage Hulk was again unleashed on the world. Banner was seemingly killed when Onslaught was destroyed, but like all of the other heroes who had seemingly sacrificed their lives, Banner had actually been transported to the Counter-Earth pocket dimension created by Franklin Richards.[316][317]

In this new pocket universe, Banner and the other heroes were reborn. He lived a new life where he had gone to State University with Reed Richards, Victor von Doom, Tony Stark, and Hank Pym. Along with Tony's friend, Conner "Rebel" O'Reilly, they formed the Atomic Knights of the Round Table. Banner worked with them on an exosuit project; however, none of them could decide how to use it. Banner shifted his focus to gamma radiation research instead. After graduating from university, he began working for Stark Industries.[318]

Stark Industries became a target of the terrorist organization Hydra, secretly funded by Victor von Doom. At the time, Banner was creating a Gamma Bomb for the military which Hydra set off with Banner still inside it. The resulting explosion mutated Banner into a new incarnation of the Hulk. He clashed with Stark in his new persona as Iron Man.[319] Hulk escaped and was later manipulated by Loki to attack the newly formed Avengers at their Avengers Island headquarters. The battle injured many of their members, decimated their base, and caused a breach in its power supply, the powerful gamma core.[320] Hulk aided the Fantastic Four, Iron Man, and the Avengers in containing the breach and saving the Eastern United States from destruction.[321][322]

Hulk and his cousin, Jennifer Walters, sought the aid of Leonard Samson to find a means to stabilize Hulk's mutation. Samson, who had also been mutated by gamma rays, received a blood transfusion in order to stabilize his mutation, and Jennifer impulsively took a blood transfusion as well, mutating herself into the She-Hulk. They joined together as the Hulkbusters and offered their services to Tony Stark.[323] Hulk aided the world's heroes in stopping Galactus.[324][325][326][327] Hulk also aided the world's heroes when the Counter-Earth dimension was briefly merged with a universe from a distant cosmos (designated Earth-50) to create Earth-13031 and prevented an invasion from the Skrulls and the Negative Zone before the proper status quo was restored.[328][329][330][331]

Back on Earth[]

While Banner was reborn into a new life on Counter-Earth, Savage Hulk, again freed from Banner, still existed independently on Earth. Hulk's body began giving off gamma radiation levels equal to those of a nuclear bomb. The Army found out that anything that came within five feet of him would be melted by the gamma radiation. Betty showed up and Hulk broke free. Moments later, Jason the Renegade stepped out from the shadows and shot Hulk with a Pantheon gun, which caused the soldiers to panic and begin shooting. Hulk laughed off the bullets and escaped with Janis, leaving Betty in tears.[332] The Pantheon had become a democracy by now and had outvoted Paris to bring Hulk back into the group. Paris approached Henry Peter Gyrich with a proposition to take down Hulk for good. The Pantheon attacked Janis and appeared to kill Hulk, but what he really destroyed was actually nothing more than a mindless cloned body that the Pantheon had created. Hulk destroyed their ship and headed towards Washington, D.C. with Janis, where she told the military that Hulk would not run any longer. If they attacked him, then he would attack a major city in retaliation.[333]

While he was traveling through the Midwest, Hulk and Janis were attacked by the Thunderbolts, whom he easily defeated. He then destroyed a dam to fulfill his promise of retaliation. Hulk began having chest pains that would force him to keel over in pain, although at the same time he was physically becoming more powerful. Doctor Strange found that because of his split from Banner, excess energy from an alternate universe was channeling through him that could destroy the universe.[334]

Under extreme emotional stress, Hulk returned to Desert Base where he had been created. He was ambushed by the newest person placed in charge of capturing Hulk, Colonel Cary St. Lawrence. Hulk considered this the ultimate invasion of privacy because he considered Desert Base "his place." He was about to kill her when he had the idea to take over an island in the Florida Keys, which he renamed Hulk Island. He saved the inhabitants from a hurricane, and they grew to respect him.[335] A few days after the hurricane, Janis showed up with an alternate incarnation of the Hulk who had come to Earth when Hulk was teleported away by Doctor Strange. He offered his help to Hulk, but the shrapnel in his brain was making him angry at everything; thus, he fought him until he was taken back to his own time.[336]

Horseman of Apocalypse[]

Hulk was manipulated by Apocalypse into becoming War, one of his Horsemen. Hulk agreed to serve Apocalypse if he would remove the shrapnel from his brain. As War, he battled the Absorbing Man and the Juggernaut, but they had been sent by the New World Order with Rick and Janis to stop this new incarnation of the Hulk, who was using the power of the Celestials. He nearly killed Absorbing Man and Juggernaut, but Rick jumped in and Hulk swung at him. Seeing the crippled body of his best friend caused Hulk to break free of the mind control and flee the scene in shame.[337]

The alien Mercy sensed Hulk's desire for death and sent him on a path to fight Mister Hyde, but Hulk wanted a good death and refused to be killed by a foe that he considered to be unworthy. Wanting to help put Hulk out of his misery, Mercy sent him to one of his deadliest enemies, Abomination. Sulking through New York, Hulk found Abomination, but because of all the damage done to his own brain, he hallucinated that he was in Abomination's place and began letting out all of his built-up rage from the last few months on him.[338]

Heroes Reborn: The Return[]

By this point, the Celestials had come to judge which universe would live and which one would die: Universe-616 or Franklin Richards' Counter-Earth pocket dimension. They sent their agent, Ashema, to Earth to show Franklin Richards his handiwork and force him to choose between one world and another.[339]

At this point, Hulk on Earth-616 was on a rampage through New York City, bringing Doc Samson, Hercules, Spider-Man, and the Thunderbolts together to try and stop him. Meanwhile, on Counter-Earth, the Banner-Hulk was on a rampage through New York City as well as clashing with both the Thing and Thor. Doctor Strange found a link between the trans-dimensional energies coming from Hulk's body and from Franklin Richards' mysterious blue ball. Bringing the ball into close proximity to Hulk caused both him and Spider-Man to be transported to Counter-Earth; there, the two Hulks clashed, attracting the attention of the Fantastic Four, the Avengers, and Doctor Doom. It was decided that to save both realities from destruction, all of the Earth-616 heroes would have to return to their native world. Both Hulk and Banner were brought back with them. When they breached the gulf between both worlds, Hulk and Banner were merged back together again.[340]

Self-Destruction[]

After finally being reunited with Banner, Hulk was transported to the site of his birth, the Gamma Bomb test site. The strain on his body was slowly killing him, and he was giving off massive amounts of gamma radiation that were sufficient enough for the Maestro to absorb it and return to life. The Maestro was taken by trolls to be the newest mind to inhabit the Destroyer armor.[341] Banner and Ross were attacked by the Destroyer and its troll minions. During the battle, the Destroyer stepped in a pool of Hulk's blood. It recognized that Hulk and Maestro were the same being and drew Hulk's mind inside of it. Hulk was able to outsmart the Maestro and crush him under a rockslide. Banner was brought back to Gamma Base, where he established some kind of control over Hulk, started rebuilding his life with Betty, and made peace with her father, Ross.[342]

Later, the Troyjans attacked and Banner agreed to meet with their leader, Lord Arm'Cheddon. After seeing Banner leave with the aliens, the press believed that he had heroically sacrificed himself to save the President's daughter. Arm'Cheddon wanted Hulk's help in resurrecting his son, Trauma, with the device that the Leader had previously used to return Marlo to life. The device needed a very large gamma power source in order to work and he planned on sacrificing Hulk to do it. Banner refused, but Hulk agreed and stepped into the machine. During the process, however, Hulk gave off too much radiation and incinerated Trauma's body. Arm'Cheddon agreed to live in peace out of fear of punishment from the Silver Surfer, but after Hulk left, he leveled Freehold and killed everyone living there, including the gamma beings Jailbait and Hotshot. Banner was given a secret pardon for his crimes as the Hulk for saving the President's daughter.[343]

The Second Death of Betty Banner[]

Just when everything had started to go right for Hulk, Betty nearly died due to gamma radiation poisoning that resulted from her time with Hulk. Banner was able to find a cure using his blood in a transfusion, but then Betty was pushed over the edge by the transfusion when the Abomination secretly switched it with his blood instead as revenge. Banner went insane and tried to kill himself seconds after Betty was pronounced dead. Doc Samson stopped Banner, but he later transformed into the Hulk and escaped from Gamma Base. Banner began coming up with elaborate scenarios to kill himself, but he would always transform into the Hulk seconds before death.[344]

With Betty dead and Banner believed to have killed her, Ross again started to hunt Hulk. Banner figured out the truth behind Betty's death when he went to the homeworld of Uatu the Watcher and was given infinite knowledge. He returned to Earth to get revenge on Abomination, but instead he let him go. Confronting Ross, Banner told him that they were both to blame for Betty's death.[345]

A Mental Cure[]

Due to the deteriorating effects of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and the chaos ravaging his mindscape,[114] Banner struck a deal with Hulk's three dominant personalities - the Green Hulk, the Gray "Joe Fixit" Hulk and the "Professor" - essentially to time-share their existence in return for stabilizing his fractured psyche and providing him with a release from his disease.[94] Despite the intervention of General John Ryker,[346] Banner was able to retain control until the Leader provided the means to cure Banner,[347] using genetic samples taken from the corpse of Brian Banner and added to Hulk's DNA by Ant-Man. The transformation back into Banner triggered a catalytic reaction that repaired the damage to Banner's cellular structure and cured the disease.[348]

The original four Defenders, including Hulk, re-formed when Yandroth surfaced again to menace the world. Though the heroes defeated his plan, Yandroth had used his sorcery to set a deathbed curse on their heads, binding them to always come together in times of crisis.[349] The curse magnified the egos of the quartet until they became mentally unstable. They then became the Order, seeking to end all threats to Earth by taking control of it. Other heroes fought them, and the energies unleashed by the battle were harnessed to both resurrect and further empower Yandroth. Coming to their senses, the Defenders stopped fighting and Yandroth was reverted back to his human form, defeated, and imprisoned.[350]

Planet Hulk[]

Banner sought refuge and peace in Alaska, where he lived as a hermit loosely connected to the town community. He was eventually tracked down by Nick Fury of S.H.I.E.L.D., who required his help in defeating the Hydra space weapon called the Godseye, which could detonate all of the nuclear bombs in the world. Sent up as the Hulk, he discovered that the Godseye was actually a rogue S.H.I.E.L.D. weapon that could match the strength of any enemy. In the ensuing battle the Godseye found out that, even though it could try, it could not match the increasing power of the Hulk, since it was unable to duplicate Banner's unique ability to channel gamma energy even if it could duplicate the energy itself, and it broke down and exploded.[351]

A S.H.I.E.L.D.-commissioned space shuttle was sent to retrieve Hulk, or so he believed. Seizing the opportunity to be rid of Hulk, a group of super-genius super-heroes known as the Illuminati decided to jettison the shuttle into space to a planet with no intelligent lifeforms. Unfortunately, there was a navigational error, and Hulk landed on the planet Sakaar instead, a world filled with both barbarian tribes and gladiator battles and ruled by a corrupt empire. The planet was situated near a portal, which gave it access to several different cultures and technologies. Hulk was captured and became a gladiator. Hulk then subsequently organized an uprising, overthrowing the current regime.[352]

Installing himself as king, Hulk met and fell in love with a queen named Caiera the Oldstrong. Together, they ushered in a new age of peace and prosperity for Sakaar. Caiera became pregnant with Hulk's child, but died when the shuttle that brought Hulk to Sakaar suddenly exploded, killing millions of people.[353] Driven to new heights of rage and fury, Hulk swore revenge against the Illuminati, whom he held responsible for the death of Caiera the Oldstrong. With his allies, the Warbound, Hulk rode on top of the prow of an alien warship as it set its course for Earth.[21]

World War Hulk[]

Reaching the Moon, Hulk defeated the Illuminati member Black Bolt - who was actually a Skrull impersonating Black Bolt, not the real one. Hulk then proceeded to New York City, where he demanded that the city be evacuated and that the Illuminati be brought before him. As the time limit for the evacuation of New York had passed, Hulk defeated Iron Man, and Avengers Tower was destroyed in the process.[354] The heroes engaged Hulk and his Warbound, but were defeated. After Hulk became allied with Hercules, Namora, and the Angel, Ross called in the U.S. Army to dispatch Hulk.[355] Despite the Army's best efforts, including the use of Adamantium bullets, Hulk instead defeated them. Alongside his Warbound, he transformed an area near Madison Square Garden into a gladiatorial arena.[356]

Doctor Strange, mystically invoking a powerful old enemy, the demon Zom, battled Hulk. Barely holding back Zom, Doctor Strange began to exhibit some of the demon's own traits. Strange sent Hulk crashing into a building that crumbled upon him and the innocent bystanders who had gathered to watch the fight. Hulk had protected the innocent bystanders. Distraught by his actions having almost killed innocents, Doctor Strange stopped fighting and, uncaring, Hulk gave Strange a lesson in control and pummeled him into the ground. Rick also confronted him and deduced that the “Green Scar” was now a merged incarnation of the intelligent Hulk and Banner personas, with Hulk confirming himself as the dominant aspect. [357]

After implanting "obedience discs" in all of the captured heroes, Hulk set Black Bolt, Mister Fantastic, Doctor Strange, and Iron Man into the arena. Hulk then had them fight each other. In the end Hulk spared them, declaring that he intended justice and not murder. Hulk planned to destroy New York City and leave the Illuminati to their shame. Soon, a nearly insane Sentry arrived on the scene and a cataclysmic battle ensued between him and Hulk. The Sentry unleashed forces that nearly destroyed what was left of New York but, ultimately, it was a stalemate between the two. Hulk then briefly reverted to Banner, and the Sentry reverted to Bob Reynolds. In their human forms, Banner was able to knock out Reynolds.[358]

Warbound member Miek impaled Hulk's longtime friend, Rick, and revealed that he had intentionally allowed the mass deaths on Sakaar to happen, knowing that they were caused by former followers of the Red King, not the Illuminati. Hulk and the Brood known as No-Name attacked Miek in retaliation. Betrayed and enraged, Hulk unwillingly began releasing energy that threatened the entire Eastern Seaboard and prompted Tony Stark to activate a series of satellite devices that opened fire and eventually left Hulk in his Banner form, whom the devices rendered unconscious. S.H.I.E.L.D. imprisoned Banner in a facility that was three miles underground, and the other Warbound members were placed under U.S. custody.[359]

Red Hulk[]

While Banner was incarcerated at Gamma Base, a new mystery revealed itself when the Abomination was found murdered in his homeland of Russia. The perpetrator soon revealed himself as a massive creature referring to itself as the Red Hulk. This new incarnation of the Hulk decimated the likes of She-Hulk, Iron Man, Rick in his new powered-up identity of a Gamma Mutate named A-Bomb, and even Thor.[360]

Banner was set free when the clash between Red Hulk and A-Bomb caused an earthquake that damaged his prison. The potential threat to Banner's life triggered his transformation into the original Green Hulk, and he wasted no time in confronting his new nemesis. Hulk, caught unprepared for Red Hulk's fighting style, was defeated in their first meeting and suffered a broken arm in the process, but the outcome was much different during their second meeting, where Hulk found a potential weakness in Red Hulk and exploited it. Once Red Hulk was beaten, Hulk left without finding out Red Hulk's true identity; however, Banner began spending his time trying to track down Red Hulk before he could do any more damage. On his journey Banner ended up in Las Vegas, where Hulk had to team up with the Sentry, Ms. Marvel, the Moon Knight, and even Brother Voodoo to stop a pack of Wendigos from devouring everyone inside a casino.[361]

Skaar the Son of Hulk[]

Meanwhile, on Sakaar, Hulk's thought-dead son, Skaar, had arisen. Skaar was the progeny of Hulk and Caiera the Oldstrong. After Caiera's death, a cocoon containing Skaar fell into the lake of fire. After a period of time, Skaar emerged from the cocoon, appearing to be the age equivalent to a human preteen. He quickly grew into what seemed to be an adult. Skaar wanted revenge on Hulk because he felt that Hulk had abandoned him and his world to death.[362] Skaar was exiled from his planet and was warped to Earth. Skaar confronted his father, who was then in his Savage Hulk persona. Skaar was disgusted with his father's diminished intelligence. Hulk engaged Skaar in a fight, which created a fissure that endangered a nuclear power plant. The Warbound were trying to prevent a nuclear catastrophe when they were unexpectedly aided by Hulk and Skaar. Skaar, using the Old Power, sealed the containment building and saved the workers at the plant. Skaar subsequently impaled Hulk and left, claiming that he would come back when he was worth killing.[363]

The Defenders vs. the Offenders[]

Some time later, the Grandmaster came to Hulk with a proposition: if Hulk chose to participate in a game and won, the Grandmaster would bring his love, Jarella, back to life. Hulk agreed and was told he could pick a group of allies to aid him in the game. Hulk chose his former teammates in the Defenders: Doctor Strange, Namor the Sub-Mariner, and the Silver Surfer. When the time came to meet their opponents, the Collector appeared with Hulk's nemesis, Red Hulk, and his team - consisting of Baron Mordo, Terrax the Tamer, and Tiger Shark - known as the Offenders. The Grandmaster gave Savage Hulk Banner's mind and had each team member transported to the times and places from which Hulk had gathered the Defenders. Hulk faced off against Red Hulk in Atlantis, where Red Hulk pierced Hulk's heart with a cosmic energy-charged trident. Hulk was eventually revived by the Grandmaster, after which he knocked out Red Hulk with one punch.[364]

Hulk No More[]

Afterwards, Banner was captured by A.I.M. and was detained underneath Gamma Base to be used to create a gamma-powered super-soldier program that was headed by M.O.D.O.K. and backed by Ross. M.O.D.O.K. was revealed to have been responsible for the creation of the Red Hulk, Rick's transformation into A-Bomb, and the evil split personality of Doc Samson. The plot was uncovered by She-Hulk.
