To infiltrate an A.I.M. base, Jennifer recruited reporter Ben Urich to help uncover the truth, and Urich, in turn, recruited Peter Parker to aid in the photography. A battle soon ruptured the tank containing Banner, causing him to transform into the Hulk. When the two Hulks clashed, Red Hulk used his radiation absorption abilities to steal the gamma energy from inside Hulk, preventing him from ever becoming the Hulk again. As the base reached critical mass, the defenseless Banner was rescued by a now-intelligent A-Bomb.[365] In the aftermath of the explosion, Norman Osborn sent Ares to learn if Banner could still turn into the Hulk. When Ares attacked Banner, Rick rushed to his defense, but was quickly defeated. Ares was soon outsmarted by Banner, and he was locked inside a room that was built to hold Hulk. After evading Ares, Banner and Rick parted ways.[366]

Training Skaar[]

Banner confronted Skaar in the Mojave Desert. After much deliberation, Skaar grudgingly agreed to allow Banner to train him on how to defeat Hulk should he ever return.[367] Banner lured the Juggernaut into fighting Skaar,[368] and then Wolverine and Daken.[369] Soon after, the pair encountered Norman Osborn's Femme Fatales, Victoria Hand and Ms. Marvel.[370] Banner discovered that Betty was alive, and was immediately attacked by a new version of the Harpy who turned out to be Marlo Chandler.[371] The pair came to the aid of the Fantastic Four, who were in the middle of a battle with the Mole Man and, later, Tyrannus.[372] Later on, Banner saved Skaar from Doctor Doom.[373] Banner and Skaar then tried to protect Hank Pym from the Leader, but they failed in this mission.

Banner then assembled his own group of Avengers to try and save Betty.[374] Betty, who was angry with him for having married another woman, was used by the Leader to distract Banner so that he could "Hulkify" many A.I.M. Marines and heroes. Banner was captured by the Leader and hooked up to a virtual reality machine.[375] He was unwilling to leave the virtual world until he was convinced to do so by Doctor Doom, who was also trapped. When Banner escaped, he was saved from Doctor Doom by the Red She-Hulk, who was stabbed by Skaar and turned out to be Betty herself.[376] The Leader escaped and the Cathexis Ray Generator machinery was reversed, and all the radiation from the Hulked-Out Heroes returned to the Helicarrier. Banner then absorbed all the energy to contain it at the behest of Reed Richards. Doc Samson died trying to help. The Helicarrier crashed and, from the rubble, there emerged a new incarnation of the Hulk, who came to be called the Worldbreaker.[377]

Skaar now had his chance to fight Hulk at last. During the confrontation, Hulk rescued innocent bystanders that were endangered by their fight. Skaar reacted to this act of compassion by ceasing his assault, but Hulk continued his, causing Skaar to revert to human form. Hulk was reminded of Banner's own abusive father, Brian, and reverted to human form as well, recognizing that he would never be able to continue the fight without Bruce Banner becoming Brian Banner in the process. Banner apologized and hugged his son, and Skaar accepted his love.[378]

Red Hulk set himself up in the White House, planning to take over America. However, Hulk showed up to foil his plan. After having Ross imprisoned in Gamma Base, Steve Rogers released him to stop the Leader and M.O.D.O.K.'s joint contingency plan called Scorched Earth. Banner was put in charge of countering the program and learned how to shut it down with clues from a de-powered M.O.D.O.K. Banner assisted Red Hulk and shut down the Living Supercomputer running Scorched Earth, not knowing that this was actually a distraction created by M.O.D.O.K., who had been returned to his human form of George Tarleton, to cover the trail of his clone and his successor, M.O.D.O.K. Superior.[379]

Hulk Family[]

The Hulk family, composed of Skaar, Korg, A-Bomb, Hulk, She-Hulk, Savage She-Hulk, and Red She-Hulk all went into seclusion, ignoring the attempts of the government to bring them out of hiding. Hulk's other son and Skaar's twin brother, Hiro-Kala, set his sights on Earth, planning to destroy it along with the Microverse world of K'ai. Hiro-Kala was confronted by his father. Skaar used his own Old Power to seal Hiro-Kala in a sphere of stone. Hiro-Kala was merged with the Worldmind to create a miniature sun so that the Old Power could be used to warm K'ai.[380]

After a wishing well's power was unleashed, Hulk found himself facing some of his mightiest foes. One of them was the alien warlord Arm'Cheddon. He defeated and de-powered She-Hulk and A-Bomb as part of his scheme of revenge against Hulk. He then revealed that he had reconfigured his power-channeling abilities so that he could channel Hulk's energy; the stronger Hulk got, the stronger he got. When the Red She-Hulk interfered with the conflict, he hit her with the full force of his power. In a rage, Hulk defeated Arm'Cheddon.[381]

Fear Itself[]

When the Serpent was freed by Skadi, he called seven hammers to Earth.[382] Hulk was transformed by one of these seven hammers, becoming one of the Worthy: Nul, Breaker of Worlds.[383] Rampaging through South and Central America, which led to a conflict with the Avengers,[384][385] Nul was eventually transported to New York City where, teaming up with the Thing, who had also been transformed by one of the seven hammers into one of the Worthy: Angrir, Breaker of Souls, the two began battling a lonesome Thor.[386] After defeating the Thing, Thor stated that he never could beat Hulk, and instead removed him from the battle by launching him into Earth's orbit, after which Thor collapsed from exhaustion.[387]

Landing in Romania, Nul immediately began heading for the base of Dracula, the Lord of Vampires. Opposed by Dracula's forces, including a legion of monsters, Nul was seemingly unstoppable.[388] Only after the intervention of Raizo Kodo's Forgiven was Nul briefly slowed down.[389] Ultimately, Nul made his way to Castle Dracula, where the timely arrival of Kodo and the Forgiven member Inka, disguised as Betty, was able to throw off the effects of Nul's possession. Throwing aside the hammer, Hulk regained control, and promptly left upon realizing "Betty's" true nature.[390] Claiming that he wanted to be alone, Hulk somehow appeared to separate himself from Banner and disappeared.[391]

Asunder[]

In truth, Hulk had resorted to consulting Doctor Doom to separate himself from Banner, resulting in Doom removing the portion of the brain controlled by Banner and moving it to a gamma-free cloned body of Banner.[392] Hulk moved underground, where he lived with a tribe of Moloids until Commander Amanda von Doom contacted him for help to hunt down a now-insane Banner.[393]

Hulk helped the Mad Squad (Commander Doom's team) to assault an island which Banner used as a base, where he was creating gamma-mutated animals in a series of experiments to become Hulk again. The attack resulted in Banner's vaporization in a Gamma Bomb, which resulted in Banner again sharing Hulk's mind, but still with his insane mind, and Hulk refused to have any memories of his time as Banner. With the transformation shifted so that Hulk was now the "dominant" persona, reverting back to Banner when he became too calm, Banner led Hulk to a journey in different locations around the world, including an old Russian space station, the City of Sasquatches (there, he protected the Sasquatches from Kraven the Hunter), and an old S.H.I.E.L.D. base, which ended with Hulk waking up strapped to a chair with a needle pointed above him and Banner talking to him on a video screen. The recording of Banner revealed that he had finally discovered the cure for Hulk, the components of which being what Hulk had been gathering throughout his "journey;" however, Banner also revealed that he was no longer interested in controlling Hulk, having come to recognize that he was a better person with Hulk than he would have been without him. This prompted the two personas to join forces again to investigate Doom's latest plan, using the gamma cure that Banner had devised to restore the animals on Banner's former island headquarters back to normal.[394]

A Weapon of S.H.I.E.L.D.[]

Banner's reunion with his persona as Hulk caused a reversion of Hulk's intelligence. While spending time alone in the American desert, Hulk was caught in the middle of a conflict between the Army and Aquarius of the Zodiac.[395] Hulk brought the Avengers a piece of Aquarius' suit that he had torn from the villain to investigate his identity, and he remained with the Avengers to confront the Zodiac,[396] as well as Thanos the Mad Titan, who revealed himself to be the group's master.[397] Hulk additionally assisted the Avengers during their war against Cyclops and the Phoenix Five.[398]

After officially returning to the Avengers' ranks,[399] Banner approached S.H.I.E.L.D. to offer them a new way to put both his and Hulk's abilities at their service. Banner's intelligence could be used to create new technology for the betterment of humanity, and Hulk's strength could be used against S.H.I.E.L.D.'s enemies. During his tenure working for S.H.I.E.L.D., Hulk battled the Quintronic Man[400] and Byzantine.[401] Hulk even became part of S.H.I.E.L.D.'s secret splinter branch named T.I.M.E. to fight a group of time-travelers called the Chronarchists, who intended to reshape history in their own image.[123]

Incursions[]

While serving with the Avengers, Banner began to grow suspicious of Tony Stark. During an incident with an alternate reality team of Avengers, Banner learned of the impending death of the Multiverse. Finally putting all the pieces together, Banner realized that the Illuminati had reconvened despite all that they had done to him. Furious, he confronted Stark, using tranquilizers to prevent himself from transforming into the Hulk. Backed into a corner, Stark was forced to reveal all that he knew about the incursions and the Illuminati's actions in fighting them. Seeing no other solution, Banner agreed to join the Illuminati in their work, protecting Earth in secret while looking for the answers to saving the Multiverse.[402] While with the Illuminati, Banner designed a device that would allow him to control when, and to what degree, he turned into the Hulk. Shortly after joining the group, they faced an incursion with Earth-4290001. The heroes of this reality, the Great Society, had also been fighting the incursions but, like the Illuminati, had run out of ways to avert an incursion without bloodshed. The two groups met to discuss what to do next, but tensions between the two groups flared up, and a battle for the survival of their respective Earths began.[403]

The Great Society quickly took the upper hand. Banner fought their leader, Zoran the Sun God, but despite fully unleashing the Hulk, he was defeated and knocked unconscious. The Illuminati won the fight when Doctor Strange unleashed an eldritch horror which killed the Great Society. With no other choices left, the Illuminati debated whether to destroy the other Earth. None of them were either willing or able to pull the trigger, until Namor the Sub-Mariner took the matter out of their hands and did it himself. Tensions between Namor and Black Panther spilled over, with the two of them nearly killing each other before Banner separated them. After confessing that he had been behind the destruction of Wakanda at the hands of Thanos's forces, Namor left the group.[404][405] Facing another incursion immediately afterwards, the Illuminati resolved to die with their world. Banner travelled to the place where he had first become the Hulk, buying a six-pack of beer and declaring that this was how he would finally be rid of his alter ego forever. When their world survived despite the timer reaching zero, the Illuminati reconvened, debating what this meant. They were unaware that Namor had released the Illuminati's prisoners, formed the Cabal, and razed the other Earth.[406]

Doc Green[]

One of Banner's own S.H.I.E.L.D. assistants, Melinda Leucenstern, shot him in the head while acting on the orders of the Ancient Order of the Shield because they determined that he was going to cause an extinction-level event.[407] Having suffered severe brain damage,[408] Banner was eventually cured by Tony Stark using the Extremis virus, which further increased Banner's mental capacity as a side effect.[409] Not long after this, Hulk and many other heroes were exposed to countless secrets that had been kept by the late Uatu the Watcher.[410] The vision that Banner had witnessed made him mistakenly believe that Stark was directly responsible for him becoming the Hulk, since he had secretly tampered with the shielding of the Gamma Bomb on behalf of Ross.[117] As part of his misguided revenge attempt against Iron Man, Banner used his new intellect to tweak the Extremis dose in his body and unleash a new persona for the Hulk, the super-intelligent Doc Green.[117] Doc Green eventually made peace with Stark after learning that the Gamma Bomb's original shielding had been over-bolstered, and thus Stark's tampering had actually refined the bomb's explosive potential so that it would not disintegrate everyone within the blast radius, with the result having been that Stark's actions had actually saved both Banner's life and the lives of everyone at the test site.[118]

After coming to the conclusion that the world was in danger due to its many Gamma Mutates, Doc Green determined that they needed to be neutralized. He developed a serum made from Adamantium nanobots that absorbed gamma energy[17] and used it to de-power A-Bomb,[411] Skaar,[412] the Red She-Hulk,[407] the Gamma Corps,[413] and finally, Red Hulk.[414] The only Gamma Mutate that Doc Green did not de-power was She-Hulk, since he determined that she was the only Gamma Mutate whose life had been genuinely improved by her condition. Doc Green additionally realized that his intellect was slowly declining and would eventually return to its normal levels, those of the original primality of the Hulk.[415]

Time Runs Out[]

Despite his transformation into Doc Green, Banner remained a member of the Illuminati, now joined by his old friend, Amadeus Cho. After their actions became known to the Avengers and then the world at large, the Illuminati were forced to go on the run. While the Cabal dealt with the incursions by violently destroying the other Earths, the Illuminati explored several avenues to find a permanent and bloodless solution to the incursions.[416] After coming to an agreement with Captain America and S.H.I.E.L.D., who had been hunting them for months, the Illuminati put a plan into motion, helping Namor the Sub-Mariner to betray the Cabal and leave them stranded in a dying universe.[417]

Realizing that it was futile to stop the death of the Multiverse, the Illuminati refocused their efforts to surviving its collapse. They built a Life Raft that would allow a number of chosen people to survive the end of the Multiverse. When the final incursion took place between Earth-616 and Earth-1610, Doc Green fought alongside the other heroes of his world, but ultimately perished in the final incursion.[418] He was resurrected, along with the rest of his universe, when Reed Richards used the powers of the Molecule Man to rebuild the entire Multiverse.[419]

Immortal Hulk[]

When an experimental fusion reactor started melting down, Banner used Hulk to absorb all of its radiation.[420] However, the new type of radiation being used on the plant threatened to cause Hulk to detonate. Hulk's friend, Amadeus Cho, assisted Hulk and, in the process of saving his life, used special nanites to transfer Banner's powers to himself.[421] Even though he had become effectively gamma-free,[422] Banner started experimenting on himself with gamma-irradiated cells at his laboratory in Utah.[69] Banner's experiments caused him to become the target of one of the visions of an Inhuman precognitive named Ulysses Cain, who foretold that Banner would eventually transform into the Hulk and cause an onslaught.[423] When a contingent of super-heroes confronted Banner about the vision, they learned of his experiments. Banner became agitated, and Hawkeye shot him in the head with an arrow that was equipped with a specially custom-built point.[69] It was eventually revealed during Hawkeye's trial that the arrow point had been provided by Banner himself, and that he had requested Hawkeye to shoot him if it even became apparent that he would transform into the Hulk again.[69]

Banner's dead body was stolen by the ninja clan known as the Hand shortly after his funeral.[424] The Avengers Unity Division attempted to stop the Hand's resurrection ritual, but they arrived too late.[70] Following a brief confrontation, the rampage of the Hulk, now again mindless, was finally contained within a magical doorway of Brother Voodoo's creation, which allowed the sorcerer to enter Banner's soul and cleanse it from the Hand's corruption. Banner reverted to his human form and died in the process.[425] When Hydra took over the United States by the hand of an evil doppelganger of Captain America, its head scientist, Arnim Zola, resurrected Banner to use Hulk in an assault against the resistance known as the Underground.[426] Even though Banner refused to assist Hydra, the side of him that was Hulk accepted with pleasure.[427] As a result of a time-delayed device that Zola had implanted within him, Hulk's resurrection was temporary. Shortly before the destruction of the Underground's base, the Mount, his body deteriorated and he died again.[427] Banner's body was left behind beneath the ruins of the Mount.[428]

Hulk's third consecutive resurrection from the dead came by the hand of the Challenger, an exiled Elder of the Universe who had returned for a rematch against the Grandmaster. He related to Hulk's rage, and brought him back to life to act as his ace in the hole during the final round of a contest between each of the Elders' teams, the Black Order and the Lethal Legion, whose objective had been to seize the Pyramoids that were deployed on Earth by their masters during each round.[428] Hulk agreed to help the Challenger retrieve the final Pyramoid since Earth was going to be destroyed anyway as soon as the contest ended, and Hulk saw it as a way to free himself of the nuisance of humanity.[429] By this time Banner's persona, who had been overwhelmed by Hulk's psyche, came to the realization that this succession of resurrections was not a coincidence, but simply a manifestation of Hulk's own innate immortality.

During the final round, Hulk rampaged to the Avengers Auxiliary Headquarters, where Voyager, the Grandmaster's own secret agent within the Avengers, had teleported the final Pyramoid.[55] Hulk quickly defeated the Avengers that tried to stand on his way,[55] and he even destroyed the Vision.[430] Even though Hulk managed to make his way to the vault where Voyager was hiding the Pyramoid, Wonder Man convinced him that the Challenger was as much at fault as the rest of humanity for not leaving him alone. When the Pyramoid was within his grasp, Hulk destroyed it instead, costing the Challenger his victory.[429] Following the Challenger's defeat,[431] Banner went under the radar, with the resurrection of Hulk becoming nothing more than a rumor to the general public.[14] Banner started travelling the country aimlessly, looking for ways to put Hulk to use as a tool to bring about justice in order to atone for his own sins.[432] Around this time, the predominant personality of the Hulk became that of Devil Hulk, a repressed alter of Banner who was articulate and spiteful, but was entirely devoted to protecting Banner at all costs, and whose transformations were triggered mostly only when injured or killed, and after sunset.[433]

Shadow Base[]

Following his return, Hulk was targeted by enemies on two fronts. The U.S. Hulk Operations, rebranded as Shadow Base and led by General Reginald Fortean, set out to capture and analyze Hulk,[434] while the demonic and otherworldly entity known as the One Below All began to use the soul of Banner's father, Brian, to influence the land of the living from the Below-Place, the deepest layer of reality below even Hell itself and the secret source of gamma radiation.[90] It was because of this connection to the Below-Place that Gamma Mutates could be resurrected from the dead, since they were plunged into the Below-Place after death, and could return to the real world through the metaphysical Green Door that connected both planes of existence.[277]

Due to the machinations of the One Below All, Brian's soul possessed Banner's former colleague, Walter Langkowski, a.k.a. the gamma-mutated monster Sasquatch.[435] Hulk managed to stop the rampaging Sasquatch by draining him of his gamma energy, inadvertently absorbing Brian's possession as well.[436] Under Brian's influence, Hulk traveled to Desert Base, where he came to blows against the Absorbing Man, who had now become a Shadow Base operative. By absorbing Hulk's gamma energy, the Absorbing Man became possessed by Brian,[437] who used him to absorb all the residual gamma radiation from the Gamma Bomb's detonation, opening a Green Door that plunged him and Hulk into the Below-Place, as well as a third party interested in Hulk also present at the scene, the task force Gamma Flight.[438] In the Below-Place, Hulk and Banner were split apart,[439] and Brian attempted to make Banner the One Below All's new vessel to bring the Below-Place to Earth. After making his way through the One Below All's demons,[90] Hulk managed to foil Brian's plans once Gamma Flight member Puck convinced the Absorbing Man to make things right. The Absorbing Man funneled gamma energy into Hulk, giving him the strength to disperse the One Below All with a single thunderclap. Afterward, Hulk merged back with Banner and closed the Green Door, returning everyone to Earth.

Due to the traumatic experience in the Below-Place, Banner reached out to Betty, with whom he had not established contact since returning from the dead.[56] The Bushwacker, a Shadow Base operative who was hot on Banner's trail, killed Betty, acting against the orders of the man that he was working for, General Reginald Fortean, when she was reunited with Banner,[440] triggering a transformation into a new incarnation of the Harpy named the Red Harpy.[441] In the turmoil of Betty being shot, Hulk was approached by Doc Samson, who had also returned to life through the Green Door and sought out Banner for answers about it. Together with Samson, Hulk investigated Shadow Base and the disappearance of the body of Rick, who had died during Hydra's short-lived empire.[433] In a confrontation with the Bushwacker, Banner manifested in his Joe Fixit persona, albeit with no accompanying physical transformation.[442] While hiding from Shadow Base, Banner was attacked by a mutated Rick, who had been turned into a new version of the Abomination by his pursuers.[441] With Red Harpy's help, Hulk managed to evade Shadow Base and dig Rick out of the mutagenic shell that had turned him into Abomination.[72] While in hiding, Banner investigated the disappearance of Ross' body, suspecting it also to be the work of Shadow Base. As a result, he became entangled in the efforts of Venom to stop Carnage from awakening the ancient symbiote dark god named Knull by retrieving the codices of symbiotes left in the bodies, dead or alive, of anyone who had ever been bonded to one.[443] For a brief time the Venom symbiote chose Hulk as a host in an attempt to stop Carnage,[444] but his gambit failed and Carnage managed to defeat him anyway.[445] Carnage would then subsequently be killed by Venom.[446]

When Rick awakened, he shared with Banner and his allies the location of Shadow Base's headquarters. They assaulted Shadow Base,[447] joining forces with Gamma Flight in the process, who were coincidentally raiding the facility at the same time.[448] Hulk both confronted and killed General Reginald Fortean, who had used Abomination's tissue on himself to turn himself into a Gamma Mutate in order to fight Hulk all by himself. In the aftermath, Banner seized command of Shadow Base's assets,[73] and set out to use its resources to wage war on the human world for their abuse of the environment, sparking a counterculture movement that embraced his ideals in the process.[449]

Ascension of the Leader[]

Unknown to Banner, however, the Leader had been studying the Below-Place and managed to replace Brian as the host of the One Below All. The Leader additionally had infiltrated Banner's circles, having taken control of Rick's mind and having infiltrated Banner's mindscape by taking over his Green Scar alter.[450] During his war against the human world, Hulk combated Roxxon.[451] In an attempt to rid himself of the Hulk, Roxxon's CEO, Dario Agger, enlisted the help of Xemnu the Living Titan,[452] who used his hypnotic powers to brainwash the world into believing that he was the one true Hulk and everyone's hero.[453] In order to stop Roxxon's interference the Leader, as Green Scar, helped Hulk fight back and put an end to Xemnu's brainwashing, while also caging Devil Hulk persona within Banner's mindscape. Due to this, Savage Hulk became the Hulk's main persona again.[454] The Leader then absorbed Brian into himself, becoming the next host of the One Below All.[455][456]

The Leader eventually made his move when he used Rick to overload Hulk with gamma energy, causing him to decimate a town where he was present.[457] While Hulk was fending off Gamma Flight to avoid capture,[458] the Leader tightened his hold over Banner's mindscape, subduing Banner and Joe Fixit as well. Devil Hulk managed to break free when the Leader attempted to bring Banner to the Below-Place,[100] but the ill-timed intervention of the childish Savage Hulk to stop the conflict resulted in the Leader seemingly killing the manifestation of Devil Hulk alter. Savage Hulk and Joe were left behind in Banner's body, which was being held prisoner by Gamma Flight aboard the Alpha Flight Low-Orbit Space Station. In the Below-Place, the Leader hooked up Banner and the remains of Devil Hulk to plant-like structures for some unrevealed purpose.[450]

Hulk was later met by Henry Peter Gyrich, who was acting commander of the Alpha Flight Interstellar Defense and Diplomacy Initiative, which included authority of Gamma Flight. Gyrich informed Hulk that he would get to decide what happened to him. He also told Hulk that the manacles that bound him could adjust in size; thus, becoming Banner would not free him from them. Joe, however, was able to transform into Banner by emerging from Hulk's body like a cocoon, freeing himself anyway. Joe then knocked out both Gyrich and the guards that were with him. While trying to escape, Joe was confronted by Gamma Flight and Doc Samson, now resurrected from the dead in Walter Langkowski's body. Joe then used a gun that he took from one of the guards to break open the space station's window and flee into outer space. Joe then transformed into Savage Hulk, allowing him to withstand the re-entry through Earth's atmosphere. Hulk landed near Coney Island, where he was confronted by the Thing as he got to shore.[459] Thing battled Hulk until Hulk transformed into Banner and the Joe Fixit persona convinced the Thing to stop. The two of them then talked it over, and the Thing decided to let Hulk go.[460]

On the Run[]

Joe Fixit and Savage Hulk then went into hiding in New York City.[461] Savage Hulk had been greatly weakened after having his gamma energy drained by the Leader after he had taken both Banner and Devil Hulk, so Joe used thievery and scams to survive and tried to avoid becoming a hero, as he did not want to draw attention to himself. After witnessing two police officers harass a member of the Teen Brigade, however, Joe decided to be a hero anyway and transformed into Savage Hulk to aid the teenager. After scaring off the police officers, Hulk was attacked by the U-Foes, who had been hired by Henry Peter Gyrich to take him out.[462]

The U-Foes took turns attacking Hulk, but when Vector accidentally sent Hulk flying all the way to New Jersey with a telekinetic attack, the U-Foes searched for him. After finding Hulk, X-Ray finished Hulk off with a blast of anti-gamma rays (cosmic rays), killing him. Savage Hulk and Joe were both sent to the Below-Place and found themselves staring down an enlarged Leader, who was now possessed by the One Below All.[74] The Leader trapped Savage Hulk and Joe in the Below-Place by turning the Green Door into a Red Door and then sent various Qlippoth against Savage Hulk and Joe in an attempt to assimilate them. Unexpectedly, as X-Ray of the U-Foes constantly bombarded Hulk's corpse with cosmic rays in order to prevent him from resurrecting from the dead, Joe was transformed into a new version of the Red Hulk and used his newfound power to smash through the Red Door, allowing both Savage Hulk and himself to escape. Joe was then resurrected in the body of Savage Hulk, no longer emaciated and with cosmic power running through him, much to the shock of the U-Foes.[75]

With his strength restored, Joe easily overwhelmed the U-Foes to the point where Vector was forced to send Joe flying toward Manhattan with his telekinesis to save the lives of both himself and his team. After learning that the U-Foes had let Hulk escape, Gyrich swallowed his pride and finally asked the Avengers for help. The Avengers confronted Joe at a bar, where he was having a few drinks. As the Avengers were about to battle Hulk, Betty, as Red Harpy, appeared to aid Hulk.[463] Later, Gamma Flight appeared to aid Hulk as well. During the fight, the She-Hulk unexpectedly turned on her fellow Avengers to aid her cousin after learning from Betty that she had also seen the Green Door. Gamma Flight eventually teleported away with Joe, Betty, and She-Hulk to a warehouse in Brooklyn that had formerly been used by the Kingpin.[464] Joe and Betty then decided to make up and kiss.[465]

Later, Joe and Betty made love in a hotel room. The two then had a heart-to-heart talk, where Joe admitted that he had left Banner in the Below-Place and Betty revealed that she liked how Joe had never hidden anything from her, but became upset after remembering that he used to be a criminal casino enforcer in Las Vegas. Tired of Banner and his Hulk personas always keeping secrets from her, Betty decided to leave him again.[466] Joe then talked with She-Hulk and Jackie, telling them that he was done with hiding and that he planned to rescue Banner from the Below-Place.[467] Joe, She-Hulk, and Jackie went to the Baxter Building to meet with the Fantastic Four and the Avengers. After a brief fight between Joe and the Avengers and other heroes, the Fantastic Four intervened and escorted Joe, She-Hulk, and Jackie to the Forever Gate, which had the ability to send Joe to the Below-Place to rescue Banner. Joe was reluctant to pass through at first, but he was motivated to do so by Jackie, who passed through the Forever Gate with him.[468]

After arriving at the Below-Place, Joe and Savage Hulk separated into two different beings and journeyed with Jackie through the Below-Place until they came across a fortress that the Leader had built to protect himself. Savage Hulk entered first and later Joe and Jackie. Joe and Savage Hulk fought a monstrously transformed Leader, but were quickly overwhelmed. After coming to terms with her past, Jackie unleashed a beam of energy from her eyes that hurt the Leader, allowing Joe and Savage Hulk to separate the Leader from the One Below All and rescue Banner. After confronting the One Below All, they found out that he was actually an aspect of the One Above All, who cryptically told them the ultimate purpose of the Hulk. Joe, Savage Hulk, and Jackie then fled the Leader's crumbling fortress with the Leader and Banner. They were then met by the Thing and Walter Langkowski, now resurrected from the dead and possessing Doc Samson's body, and traveled back to Earth using the Forever Gate. Banner merged back with Joe and Savage Hulk and, after getting clothing from Reed Richards, sneaked out of the Baxter Building and into the outside world.[53]

A Titanic Problem[]

Despite making peace with his various Hulk alters, Banner was deceived by the demon D'Spayre (who had disguised himself as Doctor Strange) and decided to take partial control of Hulk, using magic that allowed Banner to take control of his subconscious for the service of an unnamed party.[469] The next day, while in El Paso, Texas, a new malevolent persona called Titan took control of Banner's body and killed a group of people, horrifying Banner and forcing him to go on the run again. To ensure that this did not happen again and discounting on his alters,[470] Banner used technology that was stolen from A.I.M.[471] to fracture his psyche into parts, allowing him to take full control of Hulk. He fueled Hulk's body with Hulk's rage, which he generated into a section of his mind by pitting Hulk against various opponents, with specific opponents generating different levels of power.[472] Banner also added nuclear bombs inside Hulk's head to kill him in case he died but Hulk lived on.[473]

After taking control of Hulk, Banner made his way toward an old Stark tech armory in Wundagore where Tony Stark had created Project A.R.K., an interdimensional portal that Stark planned to use to evacuate people to safety during a crisis. After Banner defeated Stark and a contingent of remotely controlled Hulkbuster armors, Banner passed through the portal, despite warnings from Stark that it was too dangerous,[474] so that he could find some place to live in peace and solitude.[470] While traveling through the Arterial Dimension Between-Space, Banner was forcibly pulled into Earth-122 by its version of Banner, who asked him for his help.[472]

After Banner-122 explained his world's history to Banner-616, a military force sent by President Ross appeared at Banner-122's hideout to apprehend Banner-122. Banner-616 went on to devastate it. He then fought and defeated Banner-122's former student, the Spider-Hulk, when Ross tried and failed to hold him hostage. Finally, President Ross sent his team of Gamma Mutates, the Abominations. When the Abominations arrived, the equipment that Banner used to control Hulk was damaged, allowing the Titan persona to seize control of Hulk.[475] With Titan in control, Hulk devastated the Abominations. In desperation, Ross ordered that a Gamma Bomb be used on Hulk. Because this would kill thousands in nearby cities, Banner-122 killed Ross with his revolver. After Banner-616 regained control of Hulk by using Savage Hulk persona, Banner-122 warned him of the incoming Gamma Bomb. Using Banner-122's interdimensional portal, Hulk sent the gamma energy released by the Gamma Bomb away and then entered the portal to continue his trip through the Between-Space.[49]

Thor intercepted Banner on a mission to kill him after Titan's rampage in El Paso, Texas. Shortly after Banner and Thor landed on the planet of Sakk-Reen, Sif transported Banner and Thor to the Black Hand of God, an arena where gladiatorial bloodsports were held. When Banner began overwhelming Thor, the spirit of Odin who resided in Mjolnir flew the hammer high into the air and struck the arena grounds, causing Banner and Thor to crash down into the area below. Thor then tossed Mjolnir at Banner so that Odin could enter Banner's mindscape.[476]

Odin and Banner briefly fought until a headbutt from Thor caused Banner to bump his head and relive Titan's rampage in El Paso. Odin hoped to help Banner, but he was withdrawn from Banner's mindscape when Thor recalled Mjolnir. Then, Iron Man arrived in a Hulkbuster Armor that was built using the body of a Celestial to stop Banner once and for all.[470] However, Banner was no longer in control of Hulk, causing Hulk's rage to go out of control. While Iron Man battled Hulk, Odin tried to intervene to help Banner. Eventually, Hulk's rage reached a critical point, causing him to unleash a gargantuan gamma energy explosion that destroyed Iron Man's armor and transformed Thor into a Gamma Mutate himself.[477] Due to the influence of the Titan persona, Thor became violent while Banner became trapped in Mjolnir, causing Savage Hulk to take control and battle Thor. To save Thor, Odin helped Banner retake control of Hulk by giving Mjolnir to Hulk, causing Hulk to become empowered with the power of Thor. Thor and Hulk then clashed.[478]

As part of Odin's plan, Hulk transported Thor to Asgard using Mjolnir. After receiving a brutal beating from Thor, Hulk forced Thor into Yggdrasill to purge Thor of the gamma energy that plagued him. However, Thor was too strong and yanked Yggdrasill from the ground. As a last resort, Odin was able to talk Thor down long enough for Hulk to use Mjolnir to purge the gamma energy from Thor, returning him to normal. Now aware of the truth of Banner in El Paso and having seen a glimpse of Banner's rage, Thor let Banner leave while lying to Tony Stark that Banner had died.[479]

To avoid a repeat of the Titan persona, Banner was counseled by Doc Samson from afar through a simulation for two hours each day. Banner one day discovered a coded gamma distress signal from an unknown planet. To decode and find the signal, Banner divided his consciousness into separate constructs to crew his spaceship-like subconscious. Upon reaching the planet, Banner discovered that the planet's surface had been heavily modified by super-strong beings. After landing on the planet, Banner fought hostile creatures before being greeted by a purple-skinned woman named Monolith, who apparently knew who he was and who welcomed him home.[480] Banner learned from Monolith of the history of her people, who were descendants of gamma-mutated human subjects from Earth-122 that terraformed the planet from their fights and whose intelligence was augmented by gamma energy that was sent there by Banner completely by accident.[481]

After earning the affection of the planet's people through their Godball ritual,[482] Banner planned on leaving the planet out of fear that the Titan persona would reappear and devastate the planet. However, Monolith wanted Hulk to remain on the planet to rule it, so she forcibly began removing the cybernetics that Banner had placed on Hulk's body to kill the Banner persona. This happened as the Titan persona retook control of Hulk by locking Banner in the room where he kept Hulk. Titan tried to make Hulk angry, but Banner convinced Hulk to ignore Titan's attempts to enrage it. So, Titan unleashed the program that angered Hulk to dangerous levels, resulting in Hulk unleashing a massive blast of energy.[473]

The blast devastated the planet and killed many of its inhabitants. While the surviving inhabitants fought Titan, Doctor Strange entered Banner's subconscious using astral projection, but was quickly forced out by Titan. Realizing that D'Spayre was responsible for the changes in Banner's subconscious, Doctor Strange forced the demon to undo his work. However, Titan remained in control of Hulk.[483] Monolith had secretly been siphoning Titan's gamma energy, but when she tried to destroy him with it, he simply absorbed it all back into himself. In Titan's Mind-Palace, Banner convinced Hulk to awaken and Hulk seemingly tore Titan apart from the inside out, causing him to revert back to Banner on the outside while losing all of the cybernetics that he had attached to himself. When Banner regained consciousness, he found a letter from Doc Samson explaining that Hulk Planet was being rebuilt, that Monolith had pardoned Banner of Titan's crimes, that he had explained what really happened at El Paso to Earth's super-heroes, and that Banner had returned to his Hulk status before D'Spayre's meddling, but was warned that Titan still remained dormant inside him.[484]

Imperial[]

Banner was notified of his son Hiro-Kala's death and, accompanied by She-Hulk and Amadeus Cho, traveled to Sakaar En Nevo to pay his last respects. The Forensic Hive investigated Hiro-Kala's death, and told Hulk that his son was the latest victim of a string of assassinations on various galactic leaders. Hulk and Amadeus decided to attend the Galactic Council meeting discussing these assassinations at the Fulcrum, leaving She-Hulk behind on Sakaar in order for her to preserve the peace. The meeting was suddenly attacked by what appeared to be a member of the Intergalactic Empire of Wakanda, making everyone believe that Wakanda was responsible for the deaths.[485]

Hulk participated in the attack on the planet Wakanda Prime and personally went after its king, Black Panther, believing that he was responsible for his son's death. The Skrulls suddenly betrayed everyone and attacked the Council's forces, revealing themselves to be the real culprits. Black Panther was able to resolve this misunderstanding, and everyone worked together to fight back against the Skrulls.[486][487] The Council made its way back to the Fulcrum, where it fought the invading Skrulls. Joined by Black Bolt, Hulk and Black Panther confronted the Skrulls' leader, the Super-Skrull and, after a lengthy battle, took him down. With those responsible for Hiro-Kala's death dealt with, Hulk, She-Hulk and Amadeus proceeded to return home.[488]

Age of Monsters[]

Banner eventually tried to cure Betty of her Red Harpy persona,[489] prompting a new persona to emerge and become the dominant Hulk, who was tired of the abuse that Banner had subjected his alters to and angry at Banner for trying to cure Betty. This new persona despised Banner for what he did and began both mentally and physically torturing him with his transformation. Banner was forced to live on the run and hide himself to keep others around him safe, only to encounter an abused teenager named Charlie Tidwell, who began following him due to feeling safer with Hulk. However, an ancient being known only as Eldest awakened and sent out various monsters from around the world to go after Hulk, as she wished to use him in releasing Vinruviel the Mother of Horrors.[490] Hulk fought through these monstrosities while keeping Charlie safe, but was soon seemingly met by Betty, who offered to have Eldest free them from their gamma curse, which he refused.[491] He kept on fighting the monsters,[492] until he fought the Frozen Charlotte, who had turned Charlie into a doll.[493]

Hulk sought out the help of Strange Academy's principal, Doctor Voodoo, to free Charlie. Doctor Voodoo sent both Hulk and Banner to the soul cage, where they needed to fight the Flesh-Weaver in order to have him return Charlie to normal. Hulk learned that the power needed to help Charlie was in Las Vegas, and so Banner began making his way there,[494] only to get captured by Eldest's forces who informed him that she would free the girl from the curse only if he surrendered Hulk.[495] Upon entering the Skinwalkers' Temple of Lycana, Banner accepted the deal, causing Hulk to be imprisoned but Charlie to be returned to normal.[496] Charlie came to his rescue, and stole Lycana's godskin to become her avatar and use her power to free Hulk from Eldest's clutches as the temple crumbled.[497] Both Hulk and the now-empowered Charlie continued fleeing from Eldest's monsters,[498] but when she began struggling with Lycana's influence over her,[499] Banner decided to bring her to the Sanctum Sanctorum.[500] There, they fought a skinwalker masquerading as Clea and Thor, and although they were able to resolve the conflict, the two of them now wished to be left alone.[501]

Their solitude was soon interrupted by the arrival of the Winter Soldier, who informed Hulk that various gamma-powered individuals had disappeared and advised Charlie that she had better break apart from her companion. A concerned Charlie went inside Hulk's mindscape, only to witness her hero torturing Banner, terrifying her to the point that she finally decided to abandon him.[502] By this time, Hulk had managed to take full control of Banner's body, as he had successfully imprisoned him within their shared psyche, but Banner still attempted to communicate with his alter ego.[503] Banner told Hulk that Doctor Voodoo was in danger, prompting Hulk to look for him, though he was then lured by Eldest to the Requiem Plain, where she had been siphoning the power of the Gamma Mutates to finally free her mother. However, Eldest reluctantly recognized that only Hulk could free her.[504]

It was revealed that the Chains of Eternity were equated with the door containing Vinruviel, both of them meant to imprison Vinruviel, both of them made from fragments of the First Firmament by the One Below All, and both of them meant to be unbreakable and impenetrable, respectively. However, both of them finally succumbed to Hulk's phenomenal power. Hulk then proceeded to confront Eldest, who claimed that by draining Hulk's blood she would become powerful enough to free the Mother of Horrors. Despite Hulk's best efforts, Eldest, who was now possessing the body of Abomination, managed to actually, physically rip Banner out of Hulk's body, rendering him weak. Hulk and Banner quickly reconciled, but Eldest immediately took possession of the former, using his body to free the Mother of Horrors at last. A now-powerless Banner could do nothing but watch as Eldest used Hulk to break through the Mother of Horrors' prison and devour her cadaverous remains, emerging as a darker, more monstrous version of his alter ego called the Infernal Hulk.[505]

Banner managed to get Betty and escape from the Requiem Plain with the help of Skaar, who turned out to be alive. The couple, now free from Eldest's wrath, relocated themselves in a quiet suburban town and started using the indenties of David Hamilton and Heather Hamilton, living in secret, away from super-heroes and super-villains' shennanigans.[506] However, this "perfect life" with Betty came with its fair share of problems. Betty felt completely useless as she was not Red Harpy any more and had both constant visions of her Red Harpy form and relapses with an addiction to power. One night, Banner received an unexpected visit from Tony Stark and Reed Richards. Iron Man harshly criticized Bruce for living in his fantasy of a normal life while the Infernal Hulk burned the whole world down. Banner said that he did not owe them anything but nevertheless he helped them out, explaining about the Requiem Plain and how he was separated from his jade-skinned alter ego, and that they should search the structure of caves to find something useful to the heroes against this Hulk's threat.[citation needed]

Personality

When I was four, I saw my father kill my mother. And years later, I killed him. I didn't mean to. But I did it. I've got that kind of anger inside. That kind of capacity. But you... you have your own problems. And your Hulk's gonna have his own problems as a result. And you may not love everything you learn about yourself. But you're not a... you're not a monster. You're not me, Amadeus. You're not me.

—Robert Bruce Banner[source]

Robert Bruce Banner suffered severe trauma as a child that was inflicted by his father and repressed it in his subconsciousness. This physical abuse resulted in the young Banner developing both anger issues and dissociative identity disorder (DID), and the early emergence of several alternate personalities.[449] Indeed, each aspect of his complex mind, concerning at least three primary Hulk identities, represents a peculiar manifestation of Banner's multifaceted Freudian psyche.[76] This condition was compounded later in life by the traumatic explosion of the Gamma Bomb that triggered his initial transformation into the Incredible Hulk,[2] and further stimulated the emergence of other aspects of his personality. Following his accident that involved the Gamma Bomb, many of his alters now take Hulk forms, though some, like Joe Fixit, can remain in human form when they switch.[457]

It was revealed by Doc Samson that exposure to concentrated levels of gamma energy brings about the expression of the deepest parts of the collective unconscious.[76] In this process, the darkest, most deeply buried sense of self dictates the subject's mutation. Particularly in the case of Banner, it stimulated the expression of a repressed fury that played an essential role in his transformation into the Hulk.[76] Banner became an obsessive-compulsive person. He finally sublimated his grief and rage over his physically abusive childhood, diverting the drives that were spawned by his suffering into the relative safety of science.[76]

Because of that, Banner is often trying to hide his emotional damage, resulting predominantly in social isolation. Banner became a highly withdrawn intellectual who was unable to cope with his emotions.[76] In the course of his life, Banner has also been pursued by the destruction that Hulk causes, which culminates in more complications in his life. However, Banner is a self-sacrificing and heroic person; for example, he was willing to sacrifice himself along with Earth's heroes to suppress the menace of Onslaught.[315] Endowed with a super-genius intellect, he is also one of the most brilliant and resourceful minds on Earth. Banner has constantly undertaken a career as a super-hero while also trying to find a cure for his condition.

However, an obscure and a malevolent side of Banner's persona has also been explored: for example, when Banner was temporarily separated from the Hulk, he was demonstrated to be extremely sadistic and insane.[507] When Banner and Hulk were reunited, Banner's standard personality came into effect again, with no trace of this morally distorted side. More recently, Banner's psyche was fractured into several domains following a particular incident involving Hulk. As a result, Banner's behavior was drastically altered, contrasting with his standard personality and leading to the unfolding of a potential large-scale event.[474] It was later revealed that Banner's radical conduct was a result of the manifestation of a malefic Hulk personality.[470]

Banner and the Hulk are frequently portrayed as mutually hating each other, but at times Banner strategically acts in full synchrony and consonance with his Hulk persona, thus giving Hulk a purpose. This underlying dichotomy was confirmed by Banner himself.[508] During the Planet Hulk and World War Hulk story arcs, for example, both acted in full cooperation, and Devil Hulk even admitted that he actually cherished and cared for the Banner persona after all. Banner has also stated that Hulk's reasoning and intelligence tend to fluctuate depending upon a number of factors at the moment of transformation, resulting in Hulk's standard persona varying from a raging monster to a more calculating fighter.[509]

Incarnations[]

You... can't... break... a... man... who's... already... been... broken.

—Robert Bruce Banner[source]

The Hulk originally is characterized as a separate entity from Banner, a distillation of his human anger that gradually develops its own personality and memories separate from Banner's. Banner suffers from dissociative identity disorder (DID), which stems from the physical abuse that he suffered as a child. Banner also has developed anger issues from said physical abuse. Hulk has many incarnations, each representing a different aspect of Banner's psyche; there are hundreds or possibly thousands of other personalities of the Hulk, but only a few major versions have been seen to date.[52]

  • Robert Bruce Banner - Robert Bruce Banner is the emotionally repressed core personality, possessed of a genius-level intellect. Banner can transform into the different versions of the Hulk, whereas his alter egos seem to be able only to transform into Banner.[52]
  • An Unnamed Hulk - After being resurrected, a previously unseen Hulk persona emerged, full of mindless rage and bloodlust. He was defeated by the Avengers[427] and was suppressed by Devil Hulk, who imprisoned him in the depths of Banner's subconscious.[433] However, due to Devil Hulk having been recently imprisoned himself,[454] this unnamed Hulk persona may now be free.


  • Devil Hulk/Immortal Hulk - This variation of the Hulk persona originated as a response to Banner's need for a protective father figure. Due to his physically abusive childhood, he was unable to imagine the idea of love without pain, so Devil Hulk took the form of a demonic reptilian monster within Banner's mind.[510][433] The trauma of Banner's death during the Second Superhuman Civil War[69] and subsequent resurrection[428] allowed Devil Hulk to suppress the other Hulk personas and become the "dominant" Hulk; though Savage Hulk persona could still resurface if he was enraged enough.[90][433][511] He is extremely articulate, smart and cunning. For the most part, he acts in response to people that cause harm to others, and dispenses judgment on them mercilessly.[432] Unlike previous Hulks, he is content to wait inside Banner, possessing a measure of power over Banner that previous Hulks did not have.[511] When Banner is in control, Devil Hulk manifests as a gut feeling that guides him to his objectives.[432] In addition to Devil Hulk's transformation period being limited to nighttime, Banner cannot transform into him whenever he wants to, or even at the first sign of trouble.[511] Devil Hulk always manifests when Banner is fatally injured, but only once the Sun is down,[14] though he eventually overcame this weakness with help from Banner.[451] Like every Hulk incarnation, Devil Hulk possesses enormous strength but is proportionately stronger than ever. Examples of his strength include fracturing Thor's skull with only one punch following a severe concussion that left him out of the fight, sending a Celestial-enhanced She-Hulk flying for at least two miles away with only one punch, tearing apart the latest Hulkbuster armor that was devised by Iron Man, and overloading Black Panther's Vibranium-based Panther Habit, which was previously believed to be impossible. Thor even stated that Hulk was stronger than ever.[15] He also was previously able to defeat another group of Avengers which included incredibly powerful heroes such as Thor and Hercules.[429] Devil Hulk also has incredible regenerative power. He quickly healed a large hole blown through his torso,[43] as well as put his body back together after it was cut into its individual pieces. In order for a part of his body to heal, though, it seemingly needed to be in close proximity to other parts, and despite being segmented, Hulk was still able to move the separate parts of his body[512] in a manner similar to Deadpool.[513] Devil Hulk also has a desire to destroy human civilization, arguing that it is just one misstep away from annihilation anyway due to rampant environmental destruction (a statement confirmed by both Dario Agger and the Elder Goddess Gaea), and feeling that, if he destroys it his way, at least a few humans will survive.[433] When Xemnu the Living Titan mentally attacked Banner, Green Scar persona took advantage of the chaos that was created to chain up Devil Hulk, as he found Devil Hulk to be bossy like Banner's father, Brian.[454] It was later revealed that Green Scar was being controlled by the Leader at the time.[100] Despite expressing regret for letting Devil Hulk take him over, Banner still wanted to free Devil Hulk.[457] Devil Hulk eventually broke free of his prison after being angered by the mistreatment that the Leader gave to Banner and Savage Hulk, but was later killed by the Leader.[514] However, some time later in the Below-Place, while Banner was within the mouth of the transformed Leader, who had been possessed by the One Below All, Banner started talking to Hulk and, as he was bonded with the seeming remains of Devil Hulk, it is implied that Devil Hulk is not gone completely. Banner learned that Devil Hulk "left some room" in Joe Fixit because he had a hunch about Joe, which led to Joe being able to absorb and incorporate cosmic radiation into his body to become a new version of the Red Hulk and smash through the Red Door that was previously barring them from returning to the living world.[75] After Banner reunited with his other alters, he mentioned one other persona that was still active beyond Joe or the Big Guy, potentially referring to Devil Hulk.[53]
Former Incarnations


  • Savage Gray Hulk- During Banner's early transformations, Gray Hulk appeared as a child-like savage creature that shared many aspects with Savage Hulk, such as referring to himself in the third person and having the mind and temperament of a 6-year-old child. After a few nights of this, Gray Hulk then gained an average human intelligence. Some time later, Savage Gray Hulk re-emerged during his encounter with the Distorter, with his rage preventing him from being mentally controlled by the villain.[126] Many years later, after Hulk was caught in a gamma explosion, Savage Gray Hulk re-emerged once again, but this time he destroyed part of Las Vegas and fought two of the Fantastic Four's members, the Thing and Human Torch, during his rampage.[52]


  • Gravage Hulk/Post-Heroes Return Hulk - Gravage Hulk is a merge of the Gray and Savage Hulk personas. He was created when Banner tried to have control over Hulk's personality after using his Gamma Ray Projector, but the experiment did not fully work and, while this Hulk possessed part of Banner's scientific knowledge, Hulk still referred to Banner as a separate person.[132] This Hulk persona displayed the cunning intellect of Gray Hulk and the raw power of Savage Hulk.[128][515] He did not have the ability to grow stronger as he became angrier, but instead drew upon dimensional nexus energies to gradually increase his base strength level.[515] This incarnation has been identified as being one and the same with the "Green Scar" personality.[516]


  • Mindless Hulk - The demon Nightmare, in an attempt to find new ways to hurt his old enemy Doctor Strange by going through his friends, penetrated Banner's mind and discovered that his influence had an unexpected side effect; a new persona began to develop out of Banner's worst visions of Hulk. At this period in Banner's life, he had just gained control over Hulk's body, but was constantly on alert and terrified that this was just temporary and that Hulk, which he saw as nothing but a savage and destructive beast, would break free once more when the world least expected it. Far from being identical with Savage Hulk, this version was based on a nightmarish imagination made out of all of Banner's worst fears and ideas of his former alter ego. Nightmare continued to manipulate and increase his influence, allowing this dark incarnation to gradually rise to the surface. He finally became his own persona after Banner committed "psychic suicide," allowing him to break free of Banner's domination.[283] Eventually, with the assistance of the Triad, three creatures that were created by his subconscious mind (Guardian, Glow, and Goblin, representatives of Banner's senses of self-preservation, reason and rage, respectively), this Hulk gained the ability to speak and behaved much less savagely. Since then, this persona has not been seen again, and it has been suggested that he is no longer a part of Banner's psyche. A part of Hulk, with the assistance of Doctor Strange, entered the Dream Dimension of Nightmare as a similar manifestation as the Mindless Hulk, threatening to kill him. Nightmare was forced to seek out Spider-Man's help, as this Hulk was destroying his entire realm. Spider-Man eventually pushed Hulk into another realm, but he pulled Nightmare in with him. Nightmare has since been seen to be still alive, but this Hulk seems to have disappeared entirely.[52]
  • Dark Hulk - The Dark Hulk was the result of Shanzar, a Sorcerer Supreme from his dimension, possessing his body. In this form, Hulk had a black color to him and was more vicious. Hulk was freed from this form when Shanzar was sent back to his dimension by Doctor Strange and Bruce Banner's psyche.[517]


  • Compound Hulk - Compound Hulk was the result of the Impossible Man using his magic to fuse Hulk and Red Hulk into the Compound Hulk to fight Xemnu and Kluh, a deformed intelligent clone of Gray Hulk. After Xemnu and Kluh were defeated, the Impossible Man split Compound Hulk back into Hulk and Red Hulk.[518]


  • Hulk Squared/The Uberhulk - Hulk Squared, also known as the Uberhulk, was a powerful, yet brief incarnation of the Hulk. When Hulk and the R.O.B. that contained Banner's consciousness went back in time to stop the Chronarchists, they had to go back to the day of Hulk's origin.[124] When they did, Hulk got bombarded with a double dose of gamma radiation and the R.O.B. had to download his mind into the past Banner to prevent himself from being erased from the timestream. It is not known if Hulk Squared was stronger than Green Scar, but it appeared as if that was the case. He was so strong that he was able to unleash powerful shock waves just by waving his arms around. Hulk Squared's intelligence was like that of the Mindless Hulk's: never speaking a word, simply grunting and roaring. When Banner realized the severity of the situation, he manipulated one of the Chronarchists' armor so that he could go back seconds before the Gamma Bomb exploded, exposing him to gamma radiation again. He and Hulk Squared briefly fought before Banner had to shatter the time barrier in order to snap time back to its status quo.[122]


  • Doc Green/Ωmega Hulk - An incarnation similar to the Merged Hulk, as it retains Banner's intellect and Hulk's vast strength. It was created when Banner tweaked the Extremis virus which had repaired his brain. It is considerably powerful, being able to destroy Tony Stark's mansion with a single thunderclap,[519] and resist sonics and repulsors that were powerful enough to power a continent.[113] This incarnation also fabricated a time tunnel platform to teleport into Kang the Conqueror's Trophy Room at the edge of space-time, and easily ripped apart pure Adamantium from an inert Ultron shell with his bare hands.[17] Doc Green has recurring dreams of his alternate reality counterpart's Maestro persona, potentially suggesting that Doc Green is an early manifestation of the Maestro.[520] However, the days of Doc Green's existence were numbered. It was discovered that the effects of the Extremis virus were diminishing, Doc Green's intellect was slowly and extremely reverting back to his regular Hulk persona, and at some point in the future it would be no more.[521] Doc Green came up with an Extremis supplement that could maintain his intellect for decades, but decided not to use it, fearing that it could ultimately unleash his Maestro persona.[415] By the time the universe was restored, the Doc Green persona had vanished, and Hulk had returned to his regular self.[420]


  • Kluh - When the moral axis of numerous heroes was inverted during the casting of a spell meant to defeat the Red Onslaught, Hulk reverted from Doc Green to his simple-minded persona, but unleashed a new one called "Kluh" ("Hulk" spelled backwards) who was filled with sadness after the Avengers confronted him when he tried to prevent them from killing the Red Skull. Kluh described himself as "Hulk's Hulk" and had black skin with red lines in it and a white mohawk. This incarnation possessed incredible power: he easily defeated his fellow Avengers shortly after emerging,[36] and hit Sam Alexander with enough force to send him flying from Arizona in the United States to Paris, France.[522] As Kluh, Banner possessed a normal intellect, spoke informally, and all that he wanted was to cause destruction and "bathe in the blood of the innocent."[36] When fighting Sam Alexander, Kluh showed a tendency towards cannibalism, attempting to bite off and eat the young hero's arm.[522] This persona was lost when Hulk was reverted by the reversion spell cast by both the Scarlet Witch while possessed by the spirit of Daniel Drumm and Doctor Doom.[523]
  • Titan - Through a Green Door, the demon D'Spayre was given a speck of power from an infantile Leader effigy, which he then planted inside Banner's mind. D'Spayre described it as overwhelming and coming from a source that was far more powerful than anything that he had ever encountered.[484] Before Banner took control of his subconscious using magic,[483] a new malicious persona emerged, seized control of Banner, and destroyed El Paso, Texas. This turned Banner against the Hulk,[524][470] who imprisoned Savage Hulk in his mindscape and took over his Hulk body.[474] Impersonating Betty, the persona would seize control of the Starship Hulk and caused said Hulk's bodily frame to mutate into a monstrous form named Titan. Out of desperation, Banner unleashed Savage Hulk, who defeated the entity before Banner re-imprisoned him.[49] Despite his defeat, Titan survived and continued to communicate with Banner disguised as Betty.[476] Titan was able to take control of the Hulk again by disguising himself as Brian Banner to psychologically mess with Banner's mind before trapping him in the room where he kept Savage Hulk.[473] Titan was able to infect others with Banner's rage, causing them to lose control, as well as take control of Banner's body and give him unnatural strength without any need of transforming.[470] When Titan was in control of the Hulk, Hulk grew to at least 30 feet in height and his skin became black with rock-like protrusions jutting out from his shoulders that volcanically erupted energy. At his maximum rage, Titan in most any form could unleash blasts of energy from his eyes.[49] Titan could also kill other Gamma Mutates by sucking out all of their gamma energy.[483] Though Titan was seen to have been destroyed and its remnants were seen to have been collected by a facsimile of the Leader, Doc Sasquatch believed that it was still inside Banner.[484]
  • Fractured Son - A recent addition to the kaleidoscope that is Banner's tormented psyche, this one was begotten of the subjugation and abusing of the Hulk and, in Banner's own words, a recent inability on Banner's part to differentiate between himself and his voluminous alter egos as of late.[508] Like Devil Hulk, the Fractured Son was undying and capable of resurrecting himself once upon Banner's death; also proving to be as brutally crafty and meticulous in his vocal phrasing[525] and being every bit as visceral and flagrant, if not twice as voracious, than Devil Hulk in the application of his gamma-powered savagery.[526] Unlike most Hulk alters, however, this iteration of which was far more callous and antagonistic in his relationship toward his human form and sought a means of phasing out the man that he wore as a second skin completely,[508] going so far as to make the transformations between his human form and this Hulk form as gratuitously painful as possible in order to punish Banner for all that the former tried to do to him and others.[527] Regardless of his animosity, however, this alter still went out of his way to help a wayward young girl by the name of Charlie Tidwell practically every chance that he had, which still showed that he was able to bond with people regardless of his prominent misanthropy.[528] Arguably one of the strongest versions of the Hulk to date, the Fractured Son was powerful enough to contend with both eldritch horrors and primeval atrocities and even battle it out with a fully empowered Thanos on three occasions.[526][529][530] Having finally bested Thanos in their third fight at the peak of his power as the two of them fought over an Infinity Stone, the Fractured Son left his adversary lain out after an attack from behind that brought Thanos down on all fours, and delivered a final blow after Colleen Wing stabbed Thanos in the head with her new power that was given to her by the Mind Stone.[531] The Fractured Son has also accomplished the unimaginably powerful feat of rupturing chains that were forged from the First Firmament's essence, a primordial cosmic being endowed with power on a scale comparable to Multi-Eternity.[532] Banner apparently lost this alter when Eldest forcibly ripped him out from inside the Hulk, the Fractured Son seemingly forgiving Banner and saying that he was right to have kept Charlie away.[505] The involiate Fractured Son is last seen a prisoner in his own Hulkscape where Eldest, now standing as the Infernal Hulk, holds dominion over Banner's fractured psyche manifestations.[533]
  • Gray Hulk/"Joe Fixit" - Gray Hulk worked for a time as a Las Vegas casino enforcer named "Joe Fixit". Gray Hulk has average intelligence, although he occasionally displays knowledge and intellectual ability that is normally associated with Banner. He is cunning, crafty, hedonistic, arrogant, and distant, with a hidden conscience; various psychological assessments of the Hulks have identified this Hulk as the personification of the moody teenager that Banner never allowed himself to be. In most of his Las Vegas appearances, he appeared only at night. According to the Leader, Gray Hulk persona is strongest during the night of the new Moon and weakest during the full Moon. This aversion to sunlight/moonlight vanished when Gray Hulk's night-induced transformation trigger was later removed. Although he is the smallest of the Hulks, Gray Hulk towers over the average human. He prefers to dress in tailored suits. Joe Fixit's base strength level is also the lowest of the three primary Hulk incarnations.[52] Following Devil Hulk's takeover of the other Hulk personas, Joe gained the ability to manifest in the body of Banner, with the only noticeable difference in appearance being Banner's eye color changing from brown to gray.[442] This form of Joe can operate during the daytime, which has led to his self-given nickname "Sunshine Joe Fixit."[447] When Xemnu the Living Titan attacked Banner's mind, he mentally imprisoned Gray Hulk in amber within Banner's thoughtscape.[454] After Xemnu was defeated, Gray Hulk was freed from his glazed prison.[457] While down in the Below-Place, exposure of Hulk's corpse to cosmic rays unexpectedly allowed Gray Hulk to transform into a new version of Red Hulk, presumably giving him the same powers as well as the ability to smash through the Red Door. He was also able to take over the body of Savage Hulk.[75] After opening up to Betty, Joe expressed regret for being selfish in the past, especially for leaving Banner in the Below-Place. After Betty left, Joe decided to stop hiding and rescue Banner.[467] He eventually traveled to the Below-Place with Jackie McGee using the Forever Gate, rescued Banner, and reunited with him while also retaining his Red Hulk form.[534] Joe seems to have reverted back to his gray pigmentation, as he is next seen as a prisoner in his own casino mind palace and wearing his old Scarface clothes within the Hulkscape that is ruled by Eldest, the Infernal Hulk.[533]
  • Green Scar/"Worldbreaker" - The Hulk of World War Hulk is a cunning and more powerful version than the previous incarnations, for he is initially the enraged version of the "Gravage Hulk." His rage is at its most focused due to meditation training by his ally, Hiroim. This incarnation has extremely high durability, shrugging off attacks that have hurt his other incarnations. He has had training in combat arms, including broadswords, spears, and battle shields, and is a capable leader and strategist. Another source of Green Scar's strength in comparison to other versions of the Hulk was his lack of inner conflict, if not alliance, with Banner. There were several instances where the Hulk and Banner worked together strategically, such as acting to disable Doctor Strange. Caiera the Oldstrong, Green Scar's wife, understood Banner as well, and both personalities loved her equally. This was the driving factor in the Banner / Hulk alliance. As a result of being caught in the explosion of the warp core of the ship that brought him to Sakaar in the first place, destroying the planet in the process, Green Scar's base level of strength was dramatically increased. Additionally, because of the apparent death of his wife and unborn child and of the devastation of his planet, he achieved hitherto-unprecedented levels of rage. While in a calm emotional state, Green Scar was the strongest primary Hulk incarnation.[535]
    During a burst of unexplained anger from the Hulk in New York City, Professor X attempted to slow down the angered Hulk with intense power; however, Hulk proved to be resistant to the Professor's psionic effects.[536] Shortly after winning his fight against a demonically-empowered Doctor Strange, Rick confronted him and noticed the similarity of Banner's selfless nature, since Green Scar had saved innocent civilian bystanders. Rick deduced that Green Scar at that point was now a merged incarnation of Banner and the Hulk. Green Scar retorted, "Banner is me" when Rick stated, "You are Banner", implying that the intelligent Hulk was the dominant aspect of this merged incarnation.[537] Green Scar reached a new level of anger at the end of the World War Hulk story arc after his fellow Warbound, Miek, attempted to provoke him into destroying Earth. At this level, he started to release huge amounts of gamma energy from within his body, devastating New York and causing earthquakes across North America. It would have taken but a couple of footsteps from the Hulk to completely destroy the U.S. Eastern Seaboard. If he had not let himself be stopped, then he definitely would have lived up to his name the Worldbreaker and would have completely destroyed Earth.[359] After the World War Hulk story arc, Banner suppressed Green Scar (no longer unified), preventing him from surfacing. He momentarily reappeared in battle with Hulk's son, Skarr, still identifying himself as the Worldbreaker.[378] He seems to have resurfaced after Banner regained his Hulk powers, his anger tempered from its Worldbreaker levels by another confrontation with Skaar, and was proven even strong enough to take down Red Hulk without too much of a fight, despite Red Hulk continuously absorbing Hulk's radiation in order to empower himself.[538] This Hulk lived up to his name of the Worldbreaker by destroying a world (from a direct collision with the Red She-Hulk) in the Dark Dimension.[539] Green Scar chose to remain in Banner's mindscape and help Banner mentally heal. While talking with the Savage Hulk persona, Green Scar showed an arrogant side. He chained up Devil Hulk, believing that he was bossy like Banner's father, Brian, and refused to free Gray Hulk from his amber prison, believing him to be weak.[454] It was later revealed that his arrogant persona was actually the Leader, who had hollowed out Green Scar and was the one who had sealed away Devil Hulk. He then left Hulk's psyche for the Below-Place, taking Banner with him.[100] Though Banner was eventually rescued and later re-merged with Joe and Savage Hulk as they passed through the Forever Gate, Green Scar seemingly did not accompany them. However, Green Scar/Worldbreaker re-emerged later on during the Imperial storyline, likely having stayed dormant long enough to fully restore himself after the Leader overwrote his consciousness/personality.[53][485] Now having fully reconstituted himself, Green Scar was last seen in a gladiatorial battle royal, fighting it out with every bit of anima that Eldest had ever consumed in the untold eternity that she had been body-jacking individuals, all when the Fractured Son was sent barreling into his corner of the Hulkscape by Gray Hulk, coaxing the former to stand and fight until the last.[533]
  • Savage Hulk/"Child" Hulk - Savage Hulk or, more accurately named, the "Child" Hulk is the most common version of the Hulk, and is one of the earliest known alters, existing and fronting since Banner was just 6 years old. He possesses the mental capacity and temperament of a 6-year-old child and typically refers to himself in the third person.[90] Savage Hulk is the reflection of the young child who was abused by his father, which is the source of extreme rage and resentment from which his dynamic strength is derived. Doc Samson theorized that Savage Hulk represents Banner's unfettered id, the seat of his survival instincts and childhood desires, always trying to get his own way. He is in a constant infantile state of narcissistic innocence, resulting in a simple-minded and baby-talking creature who sees the world only as an extension of himself. Savage Hulk is portrayed as a lonely childlike being longing for friendship, acceptance, and love.[76] In fact he is naive, innocent, and kind. He often claims that all he wants to be left alone, but this is because he is constantly attacked without the capacity to understand why. He really wants to be liked and is very loyal to his friends. Savage Hulk is usually depicted as green-skinned and heavily muscled with a loping ape-like gait. While in a functionally calm emotional state, or at least as calm as Hulk can be, all things considered, Savage Hulk is stronger than Gray Hulk. While angry, he has the potential for limitless strength, depending on the height of his temper.[52] He is next seen in a playroom as the Fractured Son drops in on him, becoming tersely fractious at this Hulk alter coming into his domain unannounced.[533]
  • Merged Hulk/"The Professor" - The Merged Hulk was the merger of the three personalities of Banner and the Gray and Savage Hulks.[52] The Merged Hulk was far more well-adjusted than most incarnations, as well as an associate and leader of the team of super-heroic philanthropists called the Pantheon. Despite his exaggerated musculature, the Merged Hulk had a relatively normal-looking face, resembling that of Banner. The Merged Hulk is the largest of the three primary Hulk incarnations and he also possesses a higher base strength level. While in a calm emotional state, the Merged Hulk is stronger than Savage Hulk in a calm state. However, unlike the other incarnations of the Hulk, Banner subconsciously installed a type of safeguard within this incarnation. Although in the beginning he was stated to get stronger with his rage,[540] when the Merged Hulk's anger reaches a berserk level, he will transform back into Banner, though with the mind and personality of Savage Hulk. From this point onward, he was stated to turn weaker as he got angrier.[541] It is unknown if he would currently have this limitation or not. For a while the Merged Hulk was renamed "the Professor," and instead claimed to be Banner's good side or ideal self as a personality created by Doc Samson;[542] however, the creator of this incarnation apparently later retconned this as one of the reality distortions that was created by the demon Nightmare.[106]

Powers

Banner was recently separated from the Hulk and has been rendered powerless as a consequence of this.[505] Bruce himself stated that when Eldest separated him from his jade-skinned alter ego, this somehow immunized his cells to gamma radiochemical saturation and activation; therefore Banner cannot become the Hulk, again as a consequence of this.[543]

Former Powers

There ain't many around who can describe what it feels like to get hit by the Hulk... simple fact bein' there ain't many around who can survive to tell the tale. There ain't no pain at first.
